title: Feature Request: Simulate power fluctuation to integrate better into ne energy integration
body:
I mainly want to use this component to integrate my devices to the energy integration if they haven't energy measurements built in. So the workaround is like using this  component, feeding them into the Riemann integral integration and feeding that integral integration into a utility meter. 

Now the problem is: The Riemann integration only calculates the integral if the state of the underlying sensor changes. This can have issues if using the fixed mode with a device that runs for hours like an desktop during workday or even for weeks or years like my homeserver. As a consequence the state didnt change, the riemann integral doesnt calculate the energy used so it doesnt appear in the energy panel (like my homeserver as one of my biggest energy usages).

So my idea (if possible): Add fluctuation into the fixed mode. Every e.b. 10 minutes (or another poll time) change the value of the sensor like +-0.01, so the state changed event is triggered. If you fluctuate this with switching signings, this fluctuation will negate itself out so in mean it didn't affect the real energy usage. This would help to better suit the needs if it is used for the energy integration with fixed mode for devices that doesn't change it state that often.

Don't know if this is possible in code, but if possible this would be great

title: Unknown state_class of powercalc entities
body:
Due to new possibilities HA available in 2021.08.0 and later version,  it is possible now to use internal long-term statistics, but entities must have defined `state_class` as `measurement`.
https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/sensor/#long-term-statistics
https://www.home-assistant.io/more-info/statistics/
https://www.home-assistant.io/lovelace/statistics-graph/

It is of course possible to create in `customize.yaml` declarations like this
```
sensor.ct_kulka_e14_power:
  state_class: measurement
```
or using GUI menu Configuration -> Customizations,  
but I think this should be a part of powercalc integration.

title: New configuration option needed for specific but popular setups eg. LED strips
body:
I think about mulitiplier/factor which can be used with drivers - for driver used with LED strips or even integrated low-voltage lamps (but for standard bulbs or lamps it just should always be 1, so it should have default value 1 only with option to modify when desired).
This multiplier should be used only with power data from LUT file (and not for `standby_power`).

Hardware examples 
integrated lamps (could be used one or more pieces with one driver):
https://www.ikea.com/gb/en/p/urshult-led-cabinet-lighting-nickel-plated-30260402/
https://www.ikea.com/gb/en/p/lindshult-led-cabinet-lighting-nickel-plated-10260436/
drivers:
https://www.ikea.com/gb/en/p/tradfri-driver-for-wireless-control-grey-50356187/
https://www.ikea.com/gb/en/p/tradfri-driver-for-wireless-control-grey-60342656/

also LED stips in standard starter-kits have driver and predefined length of strip (eg. 5m), but available extension sets contain only smaller quantity and in case of strip it is possible to cut strip to desired size.

It is a kind of compromise (driver power usage counted properly only in case of standby), but I think, that LUT file should contain data for 1m of strip or for 1 piece of integrated lamp (measured or calculated from measure more than one piece connected together to driver or measured strip of any length; best measurements would be in standard setup - so I mean LED strip of leghth just like out of the box or typical count integrated lamps used with given model of driver).

It is of course possible to measure only driver working idle as separate file but it really make no sense because power losses in driver  are different without load then in real work.

Some variation of that factor could be used also for groups of identical bulbs controlled always together (as group), but in such case standby power should be also multiplied.

title: Enhancements for Group & Entity Configuration
body:
This integration is usually already quite easy to configure. For some things, however, quite extensive YAML code is necessary - especially if there are many lights in a house. Therefore I would like to make a suggestion for the configuration of lights and groups.

The first proposal is for individual lights to be monitored. Instead of creating a separate platform entry for each entity, I could imagine the following notation. It saves space and allows additional configurations per light.

```
sensor:
  - platform: powercalc
    entities:
      -  entity_id: light.hallway
      -  entity_id: light.living_room
         linear:
              min_power: 0.5
              max_power: 8
```

The second proposal concerns groups.  Especially with the HomeAssistant Energy Dashboard, it does not make sense to evaluate each light individually for the sake of clarity. Whole rooms are more useful. Therefore, lights should not be created as individual entities by Powercalc, but directly as a joint room entity. The notation could look like this:

```
sensor:
  - platform: powercalc
    groups:
      - name: "Hallway"
        entities:
          - entity_id: light.hallway
          - entity_id: light.living_room
            linear:
              min_power: 0.5
              max_power: 8
```

What are your thoughts on this?

I cobbled together a jinja to create all of the sensors. Put it in the HA developer tools template editor and it creates the yaml from the selectattr() and rejectattr() conditions. Maybe it will help someone? Maybe this doesn't go here. I have no idea what I'm doing.

```
{{ 'sensor:
  - platform: powercalc 
    entity_id: ' + 
  states.light  | selectattr('attributes.supported_color_modes', 'search' , 'color_temp')
                | rejectattr('entity_id', 'match', '.*template*')
                | rejectattr('entity_id', 'match', '.*group*')
                | map(attribute='entity_id')
                | list
                | join('
    manufacturer: ecosmart
    model: ZBT-A19-CCT

  - platform: powercalc 
    entity_id: ' ) + '
    manufacturer: ecosmart
    model: ZBT-A19-CCT' }}
```
makes:
```
sensor:
  - platform: powercalc 
    entity_id: light.bathroom1
    manufacturer: ecosmart
    model: ZBT-A19-CCT

  - platform: powercalc 
    entity_id: light.bathroom2
    manufacturer: ecosmart
    model: ZBT-A19-CCT

  - platform: powercalc

```

title: Add support to measure multiple lights
body:
Some lights have very low power draw on low brightness levels. Most smartplugs cannot measure below 0.3/0.4 watts. To measure more accurately it would be a good idea to add a feature to the measure tooling to measure multiple of the same bulb at the same time. 
The tool will divide the power by the amount of lights specified.

For example when you have connected 3 lights to your smartplug and it reads 12 watt, it will save 4 watt into the CSV file.

title: Simultaneously measure multiple bulbs using measurement_v2
body:
Perhaps measuring multiple bulbs at once would allow for better accuracy of power usage. It was pointed out that the HS110 can't measure low wattages accurately, so I think it might be beneficial to measure a group of bulbs at once so that energy consumption is measured in a more accurate range of the power meters. Maybe just an n=number of lights prompt.

I'm not a coder so PR'ing is beyond me. 

You're doing great!

body:
Not sure if this is intended behavior or not (or if I've misconfigured something - I'm new to all of this), but I've noticed that powercalc groups don't seem to get the daily/weekly/monthly energy sensors that individual devices get.

My config:
```
 powercalc:
   scan_interval: 00:01:00 #Each minute
   power_sensor_naming: "{} Powersensor"
   energy_sensor_naming: "{} Energysensor"
   create_utility_meters: true

  - platform: powercalc # Bedroom Lights Power Usage Estimation
    create_group: Bedroom Lights
    entities: 
      - entity_id: light.bedroom_ceiling_light_1
        linear:
          min_power: 0.5
          max_power: 9
        standby_usage: 0.3
      - entity_id: light.bedroom_ceiling_light_2
        linear:
          min_power: 0.5
          max_power: 9
        standby_usage: 0.3
```

This results in all of the expected powersensors, as well as the following expected energy sensors:

```
sensor.bedroom_ceiling_light_1_energysensor
sensor.bedroom_ceiling_light_1_energysensor_daily
sensor.bedroom_ceiling_light_1_energysensor_weekly
sensor.bedroom_ceiling_light_1_energysensor_monthly

sensor.bedroom_ceiling_light_2_energysensor
sensor.bedroom_ceiling_light_2_energysensor_daily
sensor.bedroom_ceiling_light_2_energysensor_weekly
sensor.bedroom_ceiling_light_2_energysensor_monthly

sensor.bedroom_lights_energysensor
```

But the following energysensors are _not_ created:

```
sensor.bedroom_lights_energysensor_daily
sensor.bedroom_lights_energysensor_weekly
sensor.bedroom_lights_energysensor_monthly
```

This behavior is consistent across all of the groups I've set up, not just the Bedroom Lights group I used as an example here.

title: Restart of measurement overwrites already done measurements
body: I am trying to measure some bulbs and experience random timeouts that stops the process. To continue the process I change the START_BRIGHTNESS in .env file. Earlier version then appended the measurements to the already existing csv file. Now it creates a new file, overwriting the already done measurements. This of course can be circumvented by creating a copy of the csv file and then copy-paste but the old behaviour of appending if the csv file exists seems way better.

body:
This is a very accurate measurement as I connected 5 equal light bulbs in a group to the measuring device.

It supersedes PR #368 as there were issues with the measuring setup.

Via Zigbee these bulbs report the following:

```
min_mireds: 150
max_mireds: 500
supported_color_modes:
  - color_temp
device:
  applicationVersion: 23
  dateCode: 09-01-2020
  hardwareVersion: 1
  manufacturerID: 4447
  manufacturerName: LUMI
  model: ZNLDP12LM
  powerSource: DC Source
  softwareBuildID: "1.32\0"
  stackVersion: 2
  type: Router
  zclVersion: 1
```

These infos are available to HA via Z2M if the setting is set:
```
mqtt:
  include_device_information: true
```

In HA they are announced by Z2M as the following devices:

```
device:
  identifiers:
    - zigbee2mqtt_0x1234567
  manufacturer: Xiaomi
  model: Aqara smart LED bulb (ZNLDP12LM)
  name: xyz
  sw_version: "1.32\0"
```

As explained in the previous PR Xiaomi might manufacture these bulbs, but the label is Aqara and there's no indication to a user that these bulbs have Xiaomi as the manufacturer. Neither on the bulbs nor on the packaging. 

So any user-facing info should list them as made by Aqara with LUMI and Xiaomi as aliases.

---

Regarding the standby consumption: Even with 5 bulbs the Shelly Plug E wasn't able to determine any consumption when they are off. So the consumption is extremely low, that's why I set it to 0.05 W temporarily until I've found an incandescent light bulb (and https://github.com/bramstroker/homeassistant-powercalc/issues/371 is added).

body:
I'm really loving this extension, thank you for writing it!  I stumbled upon it because I was going to sit down and write one myself but figured I should look first - glad I did!

One thing that I think would be awesome would be to be able to have a dummy device, that is a device that isn't really connected to any home automation at all (thus no on/off to trigger Powercalc).  For example, I have a dozen smart speakers around the house, I know exactly what the wattage is of those speakers so I would really like to create dummy device in Powercalc that allows me to give it a fixed wattage and on-time (i.e., 24 hours) so it will calculate the kWh for the energy report.

For example:

```
- platform: powercalc-dummy
  friendly_name: Smart Speakers
  wattage: 5.7
  on_time: 24:00:00
```

And that would create a sensor.smart_speakers_consumed_kwh entity that is incrementing 0.1378 kWh a day.

I'm doing this now by creating switch templates in HomeAssistant and making them be on all the time and then tying Powercalc to the dummy switch, but it would be less clutter if I could just create dummy entities directly in Powercalc that performs this function for me.

There are a lot of great uses for this where people don't typically connect energy monitoring hardware: refrigerators, furnaces, smart speakers, load controls not incorporated into HA (various lights and switches), garage door motors, etc.

It seems like a relatively easy addition to your great extension.

> In case you have an appliance which produces spikey consumption (like an on/off electrical boiler) you should opt for the `left` method to get accurate readings.

Thanks

power = max_power * relative_brightness^gamma
relative brightness scaled 0...1

title: Multiple fixes for decimal conversion
Added LIFX Light LUTs (Original, Candle, Z, Plus)
body:
This pull request includes LUTs for a range of LIFX bulbs, some of which have multiple LUTs. 

Standard LUTs for the following lights are included: 
- **Lifx Original**
- **Candle**

More information is below on the LUTs for LIFX Z and LIFX + bulbs, which are also included.

### LIFX Z (strip lights)
**Background**
LIFX Z strip lights come in modular strips, each measuring 1 meter and consisting of 8 programmable zones. Customers can extend or reduce the number of strips – which causes the light to consume more or less power. It's important to also note there are slightly different power consumption patterns when more than 4 strips are attached, as the overall brightness of each strip is reduced.

**Summary**
I've measured the power consumption of the lights at multiple lengths and included an LUT for each length. The naming pattern I've used is "LIFX Z [length] zones".

### LIFX + BR30 (Nightvision blulb)
**Background**
The LIFX BR30 bulb has the ability to enable an infrared mode when the bulb is below 5% brightness. The intensity of this infrared can be customised in the app and causes very different power usage, especially in standby mode.

**Summary**
I've measured the power consumption of the LIFX+ BR30 bulb at each intensity option available (0%, 25%, 50%, 100%) and included an LUT for each of them with the naming convention being "LIFX BR30 Infrared [intensity]".

----

Please let me know if I've done this the correct way or if there is a better / more appropriate way of including the different LUTs for these lights.

title: Nested subgroups cause double-counting of power

First of all, thank you for this amazing integration. 

I am using v0.18.1. I have encountered an issue where the summary power of a group double-counts the power of devices in nested sub-groups. Here is a minimal example that reproduces this. 

First, here is a mock sensor for powercalc to measure:
``` yaml
template:
  sensor:
  - name: test_powercalc_sensor
    state: on
```
Next, configure powercalc to measure this sensor inside a nested group:

- platform: powercalc
  create_group: Outer Group
  entities:

title: Idea - Measure power using smartplug attributes. Need help from electrician
body: Thank you for a fantastic and innovative integration. I'm putting together a submission of data measurements from a selection of Lidl/Livarno smartbulbs (GU10s, LED strip, ES bulb) and Nanoleaf hexagons. Since LED bulbs draw such a low current it is recommended to wire several units up at the same time to get a measurable power reading when the bulbs are dimmed low. This means realistically you need a number of bulbs to use the [measuring](https://github.com/bramstroker/homeassistant-powercalc/blob/master/utils/measure/README.md) tool. This can be awkward and inconvenient. I have used a Smartthings plug and I noticed that while the state equals the current wattage (21W in the example below) the attributes also have useful data. This is measuring an LED light strip at full white brightness and the 21W reading (almost) matches the box rating which says 22W max. Assuming that 'current' reading in the screenshot is mA (i.e. 1.57A) then the P = VI ( watts = volts x amperes) still doesn't work as that would be 238 x 1.57 = 373W which is higher than the real value of 21W. Trying to find more info I looked in deconz and saw that the 'Current' value is actually 'RMS Current'. Note: I'm out of my depth here. I need someone with proper electrical knowledge to help and I am probably wrong. I looked up RMS Current and found this formula: Current = RMS Current x sqrt(2) = 1.57 x 1.41 = 2.2A But that making the Power (W) calculation of 524W even farther from the real value. So I am even more lost. Basically the plug itself is working out the correct wattage using (I'm assuming) the voltage and current readings. I've no idea how they get 21W from the _1570_ and _238_ measurements Why bother with this? If someone can explain the formula it means I can run the measure tests on a single bulb/device. I recently ran the measure test on a Lidl GU10 bulb. I had to use a lighting circuit with 6 bulbs to get a measurable reading - the tests took about 5 days to complete (for numerous reasons I won't go into here). It's not practical to essentially have a lighting setup (kitchen in my case) out of action for 5 days while the tests run. I wanted to see could we use the current and voltage attributes to get the power consumption when the light is very dim. For example here is another screenshot with the same LED strip but set on the lowest possible dim setting. We see that the state is registering as 0W which is not true. I just assume its rounding down. We can see there are still measurements for Voltage and Current. I'm hoping we can work out the 'real' power consumption which I assume its in the 0.1 - 0.4A range

title: Question: Lidl Lights model number
body:
I was looking at the recent PR (#598) about a Lidl smartbulb and I see that powercalc will look at the model name between parentheses. The problem here is that the 'same' Lidl bulb can have numerous vendor and model names.

For context - around December 2020 Lidl in Ireland started selling their Smart home kit. I bought a pile of different bulbs (GU10, ES27), plugs and LED strips over several shopping trips. In January 2022 they started selling them again and I again bought more to swap out the remaining non-smart bulbs.

The GU10s have a variety of names and models even though they are the 'same' bulb from Lidl's point of view. It is the bulb which can do the warm-cool mode or the 'millions of colours' mode. I believe it is this [model](https://www.zigbee2mqtt.io/devices/HG06106A.html).

According to Phoscon these are the various names and manufacturers in my stock:

**December 2020 Batch**

- **Vendor** = LIDL Livarno Lux        **Model** = HG06106A
- **Vendor**  = _TZ3000_kdpxju99 **Model** = TS0505A
- **Vendor**  = _TZ3000_quqaeew6 **Model** = TS0505B
- **Vendor**  = Heiman **Model** = TS0505A

**January 2022 Batch**
- **Vendor** = _TZ3000_quqaeew6        **Model** = TS0505B


I also checked this information in deConz and it matches.
Remember these are all the 'same' Lidl GU10 smartbulbs.

Lidl are obvious just sourcing from lots of different manufacturers but they are going to make life very complicated for auto discovery.  Is there some option for specifying aliases in the model.json (or dir name)?

FR: Alternate High/Low power settings when measuring via script
body: I am trying to use the measure script with a Sonoff S31 via HA. I am running into the problem of outdated measurements causing an error. It looks like a contributing factor is that some smart plugs only update power readings when the power has changed significantly enough. As one workaround for this, we could try to force the script to change the power considerably each iteration. Instead of iterating through (hue, color temp, brightness, .etc) values 1, 2, ... n, we iterate 1, n/2 + 1, 2, n/2 + 2. ... n. This way we ensure a more significant change in power per iteration. The downside to this would be more erratic output from the lights, so perhaps it could be an option.

title: Change values for measurement
body:
Shelly is kinda slow to respond with new values to changes of the bulb. That's why it makes sense to have a generous sleep time between individual measurements, to avoid reading the "previous value".

Since the overall sleep time is pretty generous we can reduce the sleep time for sat/hue/ct changes.

---


I further reduced the steps to the default of HA:

24 different colors in a ring with 8 saturation steps. Also I think 5 brightness steps allows fair estimations if between them.

This results in a measuring time of around 12 hours instead of 36 which I previous got with longer sleep intervals (because of shellys slow response.

--- 

I increase the timeout for the shelly. There's nothing wrong with waiting a bit longer instead of aborting - since we talk about wifi here.

Hi,

I have an old non-smart energy-hog AV receiver which is connected to a smart plug. The smart plug has its own energy meter, so currently I pull it into my energy tab bypassing powercalc.

Now I would like to also include a subwoofer, connected to a different socket using a "fixed" powercalc strategy. It would be easiest to use the plug's entity_id as the on/off switch for the subwoofer. Essentially the subwoofer would be the plug inside powercalc.

But ideally, I would get powercalc to create a media_player group that would include both the subwoofer and the original AMP. If I try to create a second powercalc meter from the same entity_id to model the AMP itself. it complains. In any case, since groups are defined based on entity_id, I would not be able to include both.

Is this possible? I guess if not, maybe the simplest way would be to allow for a config where powercalc takes a real power meter from the plug and then modifies it, e.g. by adding a fixed energy when the plug is on, representing the subwoofer?

title: Extend model.json schema with calculation_enabled_strategy:
Create power entity for Daily fixed energy settings
body:
Hi,

When the _Daily fixed energy_ is set for an always on entity such as an internet router, it does correct create the energy entity which will increase overtime with the kWh or W set as _unit_of_measurement_.

However, is it possible to also create a power entity which remains set to the stated W.

There are some **always on devices** that will draw power on the meter, but will not show up in the real time power consumption.

Lets take an easy exemple where we have something like

```
 - platform: powercalc
    create_group: Everything
    entities:
      - name: Router
        daily_fixed_energy:
          value: 20
          unit_of_measurement: W
      - name: Random Switch
        entity_id: switch.random
            fixed:
              power: 50
```

The dashboard containing Everything would only show 50W if the switch is on, and 0 when off.
But in fact, it should also add up the router which draws a constant 20W.

So we should have 20W when the switch is off, and 70W when the switch is on.

title: Add Wiz Bulb, Filament and Spot
body:
I added three new Wiz models:

- **Bulb**: A19 E26 socket with Color. Just as mentioned in the first Wiz contribution, this one has the same type SHRGB1C. Following the suggestion, I'm adding the model: 9290022656. For this one I'm guessing that any Bulb shape brother (like A60 E27)  same power and voltage in specs will be the same. 220V versions are not likely to be the same.
- **Filament**: ST19 E26 is a simple one with only brightness adjustment. I also add the specification of being Transparent since the Ambar (tinted) has higher power to match the lm lost in the tint.
- **Spot**: PAR16 GU10 has TW but is not the same than the pure Wiz branded one. This is the EVOLUZIONA rebrand also known as tecnolite in Mexico. In home assistant works with the Wiz integration and its native app. I don't expect many people to have this model but hope it works for someone.

I'm a bit paranoid so increased a little the waiting time for the measurement and also ran many plots on all colors and temps to make sure it made sense. Also compared results to some configurations manually just to make sure the measurement updates didn't come late.

Also, I went for stacking many lights vs using dummy load since I saw they added external noise and fluctuation (other lights kept dropping on power and then varying, couldn't find an amazingly steady device to plug). Better for same model bulb noise to cancel out/average and spread between them the plug error. I saw that this plug was ok with anything above 0.5W so all my measurements in idle times the bulbs is very well above that. Finally most of the time the noise would be around 0.01W and very few times reaching 0.04W, I hope the real value and calibration of Kasa is just as good (idles matched perfectly with a previous non smart measurement device).

Thanks for you amazing work, the script worked like a charm.

title: Add an approximation method for non-scanned configurations
body:
I just added a few new lights and now everything works wonderfully. However, I noticed that many light configurations in between scans (for the bri and mired steps) fail by up to 5% or more. Currently I'm using Wiz automatic circadian cycle and looking to use adaptive lighting, so my lights are all the time changing temp. 

In an attempt to fill the gaps between bri and mired steps I tested some Machine Learning algorithms and unsurprisingly the best one was K-nearest neighbors with 4 neighbors. Without getting too complicated on the final model, this simple algorithm just summarizes in a very simple approximation to the untested configuration by using the 4 closest configurations that are indeed measured. I even generated the full 77010 possible configurations using that criterion and its always performing better.

The idea is not to fill the gaps in the .gz that exist, just add this logic when making the lookup. I am guessing it can be done without too much computational effort and it’s not even an interpolation or anything complex.

I am not sure if this has been proposed/attempted before, but if you see value on doing it i can do my best on helping to implement it. Either provide with a detailed explanation on the theoretical part (no big deal) or dig into the code and do it myself.

In the image you can see (plug cyan, proposal blue, .gz purple) they start perfectly with a known configuration on the .gz, then I move to three configurations in between .gz measurements and the proposal is almost always on the spot (actually the "error" is just the plugs rounding to one decimal, otherwise they would be the same value). On this example the purples error is around 5%.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/28607630/180585292-311349cc-4be2-4640-bd41-f9f54ec41dcc.png)

title: Measurement: Allow 'resume' to be configured
body:
Where you have the script running in the background for a number of hours; it would be good to be able to set it in a loop to continually resume.
```
        return inquirer.confirm(
            message="CSV File already exists. Do you want to resume measurements?",
            default=True
        )
```

Right now it asks for confirmation, defaults to true.
Something like `yes` might be able to get past this on linux; or echo 'y' on windows; but it would be nice to just set this to a default and never be prompted.

              standby_power: 0.4
              fixed:
                power: 15
            - entity_id: light.pc_led_kette
              linear:
                min_power: 0.4
                max_power: 3
            - entity_id: light.led_kette_rechts
              linear:
                min_power: 0.4
                max_power: 3.1
        - create_group: Gruppe Schlafzimmer Plugs Gesamt
          entities:
            - entity_id: switch.steckdose_alexa_sz1_eingeschaltet

            - entity_id: switch.steckdose_pc_schlafzimmer

              energy_sensor_unit_prefix: none

            - entity_id: switch.shelly_shplg_s_87e9c7_pc
              power_sensor_id: sensor.shelly_shplg_s_87e9c7_pc_current_consumption_kw

              name: "PC Plug"

              power_sensor_id: sensor.steckdose_ventilator_leistung_kw
              energy_sensor_unit_prefix: none
            - entity_id: light.homey_on_off_plug
              power_sensor_id: sensor.dirks_homey_pro_leistung_kw
              energy_sensor_unit_prefix: none

              entities:

                  entities:
                    - entity_id: light.kuche_spot_2
                    - entity_id: light.kuche_spot_3
                - create_group: Gruppe Küche Spots Aussen Gesamt
                  entities:
                    - entity_id: light.kuche_spot_1
                    - entity_id: light.kuche_spot_4

            - create_group: Gruppe Küche LED Ketten Gesamt
              entities:
                - entity_id: light.kuhlschrank_led_kette
                - entity_id: light.spule_led_kette
            # Gruppe Kueche LED
            - create_group: Gruppe Küche LED Gesamt
              entities:
                - entity_id: light.kuhlschrank_led
                  standby_power: 0.4
                  fixed:
                    power: 11.4 #Power when the light is on
                - entity_id: light.spule_led
                  standby_power: 0.4
                  fixed:
                    power: 11.4 #Power when the light is on

          entities:
            - entity_id: switch.steckdose_kuche

              energy_sensor_unit_prefix: none

    - create_group: Gruppe Flur Gesamt
      entities:
        - entity_id: light.flurlampe

```

For what it's worth, I recently changed my YAML configuration to remove manufacturer/model overrides for some, but not all, of these entities, all of which are Hue (Signify) bulbs.  When I originally added them, there were no LUT files for those specific models, so I overrode the model number to force Powercalc to use LUT files for similar bulbs.  I recently noticed that model-specific LUT files have been added, so I commented out those overrides assuming that Powercalc would simply use the other LUT files going forward.  I did not notice an error message until I updated to 2022.8.0b0, but I suppose it's possible that commenting out the manufacturer/model overrides has something to do with the error, and I simply did not notice until now.

The power and energy sensors appear to still be working correctly, but I would appreciate any suggestions for tweaking my configuration -- either YAML or in .storage -- to clear this error message.

The relevant YAML sensor configuration is pasted below for reference.

```yaml
sensor:

  - platform: powercalc

title: Group sensors remain unavailable after Home Assistant restart
body:
I just upgraded to v0.24.5 from a much earlier version (I think 0.23.something), and now after a Home Assistant Core restart most of my group sensors show as unavailable, and stay unavailable no matter what I do with any of the groups' lights (turn on, off, change brightness, etc.). The lights come from MQTT via Zigbee2MQTT.

I think this is caused by 07a73856a15628390c450c4bc9963109f3d6b949 setting a group to unavailable if all members are unavailable, which appears to be the case for (many of) the Zigbee2MQTT lights while Home Assistant is starting up, and then never setting the group back to available when members become available again.

I fixed the problem locally by inserting
```
self._attr_available = True
```
in sensors/group.py before line 278 (i.e. just before the final `self.async_schedule_update_ha_state(True)` action of the `on_state_change` function). Not sure if this is the right way to fix it, though (as I have no experience writing Home Assistant integrations so far).

title: Utility meter for domain group not working
body:
I upgraded powercalc to v0.24.6 from v0.22.something and my utility meter for my lights domain group is now broken. It was previously working fine.

Config:
```
powercalc:
  enable_autodiscovery: true
  create_domain_groups:
    - light
  create_utility_meters: true
  utility_meter_types:
    - daily
```

Debug log:
```
2022-08-04 19:44:52 DEBUG (MainThread) [custom_components.powercalc] Setting up domain based group sensors..
2022-08-04 19:44:52 DEBUG (MainThread) [custom_components.powercalc.sensors.group] Creating grouped power sensor: All light power
2022-08-04 19:44:52 DEBUG (MainThread) [custom_components.powercalc.sensors.group] Creating grouped energy sensor: All light energy
2022-08-04 19:44:52 DEBUG (MainThread) [custom_components.powercalc.sensors.utility_meter] Creating utility_meter sensor: All light energy daily (entity_id=sensor.all_light_energy_2_daily)
```

I suspect the last line is revealing because **sensor.all_light_energy_2_daily** does not exist. The correct sensor to use should be **sensor.all_light_energy_daily**.

The only place I could find reference to the wrong sensor via a grep was in .storage/core.restore_state:
```
            "state": {
                "entity_id": "sensor.all_light_energy_daily",
                "state": "0",
                "attributes": {
                    "state_class": "total_increasing",
                    "source": "sensor.all_light_energy_2",
                    "status": "collecting",
                    "last_period": "0.4340",
                    "meter_period": "daily",
                    "cron pattern": "0 0 * * *",
                    "last_reset": "2022-08-03T14:00:00.071537+00:00",
                    "unit_of_measurement": "kWh",
                    "device_class": "energy",
                    "icon": "mdi:counter",
                    "friendly_name": "All light energy daily"
                },
```

Again, that source **sensor.all_light_energy_2** does not exist. It should be **sensor.all_light_energy**. I have tried stopping my HASS docker container then manually editing that source line and removing the "_2" from the entity_id but it does not fix anything and is later overwritten. Looking at the code maybe it is appending "_2" as a utility meter type but I couldn't parse any more than that by just reading the code.

body: Notice the word 'Again in title'.... I previously had a yaml config, in which I had each sensor listed under its own `platform: powercalc`. The startup time was huge, and almost topped the list (only to be trumped buy Mqtt) After Bram [suggested ](https://github.com/bramstroker/homeassistant-powercalc/issues/840#issuecomment-1201364325)we could list them all under that platform, like ``` sensor: platform: powercalc entities: - entity_id: sensor.doorbell - entity_id: sensor.backdoor ``` startup time was reduced to 2 sec max. Also, when debug level on Powercalc was set, the log was reduced to 1 line, where in the former config, all entities were logged individually. See that same linked issue tracker. I recently moved from Yaml to UI config. And, much to my surprise, now see this: its all back. Given the fact UI also has issues with [inheriting the Areas of the source entities](https://github.com/bramstroker/homeassistant-powercalc/discussions/983), I wonder if we should fallback to Yaml. Hope this particular startup time issue can be fixed, because that is really nasty of course. Might not impact performance, but still the time registered is not good.

body:
Hi,

I have powercalc 0.25 create the utility_meters for my lights -- most are powercalc entities, but i have a few Zwave relays which have their own energy/power measurement and which are included. The problem is that every so often e.g. the Zwave server drops out, or there is some other glitch, so that the energy sensor for the light disappears and then reappears, subtracting its instantaneous total energy used and adding it back in. The domain energy sensor goes down and up without an issue

The problem is that the utility meters only record the increase, so all of a sudden I have e.g. 90kWh used for lights on a single day. Would it be possible to get powercalc to add a "net_consumption: true" field in the meters' definition to work around this? I think in most cases, this should be fine, only if the source meter resets on some cadence this would be a problem. This is what I do for the domains not tracked by powercalc and it works fine for me.

title: Adding measured power for Nanoleaf Canvas 17PK lights
body:
I'm adding the power measurements for a Nanoleaf Canvas Stater Pack with 17 Light Panels.

Note that Home Assistant will only identify the controller as a model "NL29", without knowing the number of panels attached to it.
Those measurements are for 17 panels in total (as part of a starter kit with 1 controller and 16 additional panels): https://www.amazon.co.uk/dp/B085QTPKB8/

I've intentionally named it by the manufacture's product number to prevent Home Assistant to automatically detect it (as HA cannot identify the number of panels, which will affect the power consumption), but the model should be available to setup via YAML.

I can try to measure with smaller number of panels in the future, if there is a demand, however we still have to require users to setup this via YAML.

Hey, this PR adds support for the Philips Hue White A60 E27 with 800 lumens (model `LWA011` / `929001821618`).

Measurements were taken from 2 bulbs connected to an Aqara Smart Plug (`SP-EUC01`) using the following options:

SLEEP_TIME=60
SLEEP_TIME_SAMPLE=60
SAMPLE_COUNT=3
MAX_NUDGES=3
PULSE_TIME_NUDGE=5
SLEEP_NUDGE=60
```

Initially, I couldn't get it to run due to this smart plug's slow update time, but increasing the sleep times and enabling nudging got it working. On the other hand, some of these options are most likely unnecessarily slow (total measurement took over 24 hours), so anyone using a similar setup might benefit from tweaking them a bit more. I hope the precision is adequate.

Thanks, and keep up the great work on this project!

title: Autodiscovery not working on tp-link AU due to parenthesis in model name
body:
Hi,
I have a bunch of tp-link kasa things, mostly KP115 and KP303. I'm in Australia so they are the Australian variants.
KP115 is supported already, I measured the AU version and confirmed power profile is matching the model already existing here.

The AU version however has model id 'KP115(AU)'. This is similar for other kasa AU devices e.g. 'KP303(AU)'
I tried adding this as an alias in the model.json but then noticed the following in the logs for a KP115(AU):
`2022-11-12 12:43:54.015 DEBUG (MainThread) [custom_components.powercalc.power_profile.model_discovery] switch.fridge: Auto discovered model (manufacturer=TP-Link, model=AU)
2022-11-12 12:43:54.015 DEBUG (MainThread) [custom_components.powercalc] switch.fridge: Model not found in library, skipping discovery`

I only had a quick look so maybe wrong but I think this is due to model_discovery.py line 88, regex search deliberately grabs only content within parenthesis, resulting in model = 'AU':
`if match := re.search(r"\(([^\(\)]+)\)$", str(device_entry.model)):`

Can't add 'AU' as an alias as KP303(AU) is discovered as model=AU as well, presumably other kasa AU devices also are. 
Sure I could brute force fix it but I assume the search is this way because some other devices required it and I wouldn't want to break them :) 
Happy to provide further info or testing if it helps

title: Sonos Room/Home Theater configuration bug
body:
I'm super excited that this is expanding into Sonos Stuff!  I have a bunch of Sonos items that I'll try and meter and get submitted.

TL:DR Sonos Rooms (home theater) with multiple devices may not be appropriate for automatic configuration.

I was looking through the code and realized there may be a small problem with automatic configuration of Sonos devices that may not be clear to the casual user.  Sonos items that are grouped into a Sonos Room (aka home theater) using the Sonos app may have multiple devices, but appear as a single item to Home Assistant.

For example, I have a Living Room Sonos Playbar that in the Sonos App configuration is paired with two Sonos Play:1 (left/right surround) and a Sonos Subwoofer.  See https://support.sonos.com/en-us/article/add-surround-speakers-to-a-sonos-home-theater. In this configuration the Playbar is the 'Sonos Room group master' (not related to in Home Assistant if two media_player devices are grouped).  I have a Study Sonos Playbar that is just by itself (no home theater setup).  In Home Assistant, these shows up at two devices, not five.  Both items show up as model_name=Sonos Playbar.  The two Living Room Sonos Play:1 and Living Room Sonos Sub do not appear as devices in Home Assistant because Home Assistant treats the Living Room Playbar as a single media_player device that controls the three other "hidden" devices. 

From a Powercalc perspective, there will be two automatically configured items, both of them Sonos Playbar. In my example above, the Study Sonos Playbar will have accurate power usage. The Living Room, however, will not be accurate because there are three other devices that are not accounted for (the two Sonos Play:1 and the Sub) even IF Powercalc had information on to measure those devices.  For the casual user, this might not be clear since they may not realize that in a home theater scenario, we are not capturing the energy of the other hidden devices.

It looks like the code might be using data.model_name to determine if the device can be automatically configured in Powercalc. If I go to each of my two devices and Download the Sonos Diagnostics, I notice that one value we might be able to key off is the following:

data._last_event_cache.device.DeviceProperties.ht_sat_chan_map_set

For the Study Sonos Playbar which is by itself, this value is null

For the Living Room Sonos Playbar which has three other items tied to it, this has a value "RINCON_7828CA51498801400:LF,RF;RINCON_949F3E43A8AC01400:SW;RINCON_949F3E8B91E601400:LR;RINCON_949F3E8B998801400:RR","

In theory, this could be parsed to get the additional items somehow:
     RINCON_7828CA51498801400:LF,RF = Playbar  
     RINCON_949F3E43A8AC01400:SW = Subwoofer
     RINCON_949F3E8B998801400:RR = Sonos Play:1 Right
     RINCON_949F3E8B91E601400:LR = Sonos Play:1 Left

A Sonos thing, each entity is RINGCON_{MAC ADDRESS OF SONOS DEVICE}1400.  1400 is the TCP port that Sonos talks on.  We might wanna ask a few other folks to verify that they see this value as populated when in Home Theater mode, and null when not, but my casual scan of my 12 Sonos devices seems to show that.

Regardless, it might make sense until this can be sorted out, that any Sonos device which has a non-null value in data._last_event_cache.device.DeviceProperties.ht_sat_chan_map_set NOT be automatically configured and perhaps in release notes, we can put that Sonos Rooms or Home Theater with more than one device are not automatically configured since Home Assistant does not define the hidden devices and thus the power meter would be inadequate.

title: Integration is using deprecated `DEVICE_CLASS_*` constants
body:
This custom integration uses deprecated `DEVICE_CLASS_*` constants in its codebase.

The `DEVICE_CLASS_*` constants have been deprecated and replaced in Home Assistant Core 2021.12 (over a year ago). I would highly suggest updating/migrating this integration to the new enums.

For example, for the device classes supported by the `sensor` platform, there is now a `SensorDeviceClass` enum. So if a sensor previously used the `DEVICE_CLASS_ENERGY` constant, it should now use `SensorDeviceClass.ENERGY`. Other platforms (like `binary_sensor`, and `number`) provide similar enumerations for their supported device classes.

The migration thus only consists of replacing constants with an enumeration member and is, therefore, very low impact and should be fairly straightforward.

If I can help resolve any questions regarding this change or migration, feel free to ask or respond to this issue. I'm happy to help!

Kindest regards,

../Frenck

title: Entity not defined all of a sudden
body:
After testing the latest version of PowerCalc, I still see the same issue with virtual power sensors.
I have setup two virtual power devices which generate 2 entities (power/energy) each. In PowerCalc they show up as one device with two entities (power/energy). I use these devices as 'individual' devices in the energy tab and this works fine initially.

After a while for no apparent reason both entities of the device suddenly disappear, sometimes for one device sometimes both devices. The result is that in the energy configuration the devices are marked as 'Entity not defined' and the sensor stops working. The only way to get the sensor back is to go to the PowerCalc integration and reload the device. Then the 2 entities (power/energy) of the device re-appear and the sensor works again. However, if you had set the name of the power/energy sensor, the name falls back to the default name from Entity ID. The configured Name is gone.

Regards, Harry

title: Issue with groups and existing power sensors
body:
Hi,

I am getting some strange error messages when I attempt to create groups from real power sensors paired with powercalced energy sensors.

Am running the following versions:

```
Home Assistant 2023.2.5
Supervisor 2023.01.1
Operating System 9.5
Frontend 20230202.0 - latest

HACS:
Integration version: | 1.30.1
Frontend version: | 20220906112053
Repositories: | 1206
Downloaded repositories: | 5

PowerCalc: 
v1.3.5
```

At the highest level:

I am getting power sensors for various solar systems through their APIs, but no energy readings (don't get me started...).
So I use Powercalc to calculate an energy sensor and a daily meter for it. Works great. I have set unique IDs by hand for now (will get replaced by serial numbers of the inverters...) to ensure I have a single set of uniqe sensors throughout the custom component I am working on.

The power sensors are defined like that (l0 sensors are the JSON response from the API):

For reference I have labeled the sensors as follows: l0 ... API call, l1 ... sensor mappings, l2 ... energy calculations, l3 ... energy and power aggregations...

```
        - name: "Pionizer L1 Solax API Inverter 1 MPPT 1 Power"
          state: "{{ state_attr('sensor.pionizer_l0_solax_api_inverter_1', 'powerdc1') }}"
          unit_of_measurement: "W"
          device_class: power
          state_class: measurement
          unique_id: pionizer_l1_solax_api_inverter_1_mppt_1_power
          icon: mdi:solar-power-variant

        - name: "Pionizer L1 Solax API Inverter 1 MPPT 2 Power"
          state: "{{ state_attr('sensor.pionizer_l0_solax_api_inverter_1', 'powerdc2') }}"
          unit_of_measurement: "W"
          device_class: power
          state_class: measurement
          unique_id: pionizer_l1_solax_api_inverter_1_mppt_2_power
          icon: mdi:solar-power-variant

        - name: "Pionizer L1 Solax API Inverter 1 MPPT 3 Power"
          state: "{{ state_attr('sensor.pionizer_l0_solax_api_inverter_1', 'powerdc3') }}"
          unit_of_measurement: "W"
          device_class: power
          state_class: measurement
          unique_id: pionizer_l1_solax_api_inverter_1_mppt_3_power
          icon: mdi:solar-power-variant
```

They all work great. Getting them every 5 min.

Then I added Energy sensors like that:

```
    - platform: powercalc
      name: "Pionizer L2 Inverter 1 MPPT 1 Production"
      unique_id: sensor.pionizer_l2_inverter_1_mppt_1_production
      power_sensor_id: sensor.pionizer_l1_solax_api_inverter_1_mppt_1_power

    - platform: powercalc
      name: "Pionizer L2 Inverter 1 MPPT 2 Production"
      unique_id: sensor.pionizer_l2_inverter_1_mppt_2_production
      power_sensor_id: sensor.pionizer_l1_solax_api_inverter_1_mppt_2_power

    - platform: powercalc
      name: "Pionizer L2 Inverter 1 MPPT 3 Production"
      unique_id: sensor.pionizer_l2_inverter_1_mppt_3_production
      power_sensor_id: sensor.pionizer_l1_solax_api_inverter_1_mppt_3_power
```

together with global settings like this:
```
  powercalc:
    enable_autodiscovery: false
    power_sensor_naming: "{} Power"
    energy_sensor_naming: "{} Energy"
    create_utility_meters: true
    utility_meter_types:
      - daily
```

All of them work great as well, including the Daily utility meters.

The problems start when I try to add groups to aggregate the individual sensors at the inverter and system level.

```
    - platform: powercalc
      create_group: "Pionizer L3 Inverter 1 Solar Production"
      unique_id: sensor.pionizer_l3_inverter_1_solar_production
      entities:
        - power_sensor_id: sensor.pionizer_l1_solax_api_inverter_1_mppt_1_power
          energy_sensor_id: sensor.pionizer_l2_inverter_1_mppt_1_production_energy
        - power_sensor_id: sensor.pionizer_l1_solax_api_inverter_1_mppt_2_power
          energy_sensor_id: sensor.pionizer_l2_inverter_1_mppt_2_production_energy
        - power_sensor_id: sensor.pionizer_l1_solax_api_inverter_1_mppt_3_power
          energy_sensor_id: sensor.pionizer_l2_inverter_1_mppt_3_production_energy
```

Always result in the following errors:

```
Logger: homeassistant.components.sensor
Source: helpers/entity_platform.py:540 
Integration: Sensor ([documentation](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/sensor), [issues](https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3A%22integration%3A+sensor%22)) 
First occurred: 2:51:03 AM (4 occurrences) 
Last logged: 2:51:03 AM

Platform powercalc does not generate unique IDs. ID sensor.pionizer_l2_inverter_1_mppt_1_production_energy_daily is already used by sensor.pionizer_l2_inverter_1_mppt_1_production_energy_daily - ignoring sensor.pionizer_l2_inverter_1_mppt_1_production_energy_daily
Platform powercalc does not generate unique IDs. ID sensor.pionizer_l2_inverter_1_mppt_2_production_energy_daily is already used by sensor.pionizer_l2_inverter_1_mppt_2_production_energy_daily - ignoring sensor.pionizer_l2_inverter_1_mppt_2_production_energy_daily
Platform powercalc does not generate unique IDs. ID sensor.pionizer_l2_inverter_1_mppt_3_production_energy_daily is already used by sensor.pionizer_l2_inverter_1_mppt_3_production_energy_daily - ignoring sensor.pionizer_l2_inverter_1_mppt_3_production_energy_daily
Platform powercalc does not generate unique IDs. ID sensor.pionizer_l2_inverter_1_mppt_4_production_energy_daily is already used by sensor.pionizer_l2_inverter_1_mppt_4_production_energy_daily - ignoring sensor.pionizer_l2_inverter_1_mppt_4_production_energy_daily
```

I have tried it with and without unique id. If I remove the unique IDs, the group setup actually creates a second set of energy sensors by appending _2 to the l2 energy sensors.

Very much appriciate any guidance!

### System Health details

Sorry, but I can't find taht button on my HA Docker :-/

### Checklist

- [X] I have read the [FAQ](https://homeassistant-powercalc.readthedocs.io/en/latest/troubleshooting/faq.html) to see if there is a known solution to my problem.

### Describe the issue

I have a very strange problem where the Home Assistant Energy Dashboard shows negative values for a group created by Powercalc that includes existing energy sensors.

This is what my energy dashboard looks like:
![Screenshot 2023-03-02 205059](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7945681/222540358-513ab53b-8ea5-492f-88d9-9cd74ceb67a6.png)
![Screenshot 2023-03-02 205126](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7945681/222540374-7ca50d75-def6-439f-b8e6-d3b2e66f2f9d.png)

 This is what the part of the config for the energy group looks like:
```yaml
      - create_group: "Energie Büro & Nähzimmer"
        entities:
          - name: "Energie Büro Deckenlampe"
            unique_id: "4466714e59a64e66a254816003497341"
            entity_id: "light.buro_deckenleuchte"
          - name: "Energie Nähtisch Deckenlampe"
            unique_id: "e7326597a98a433ba995bb9b0c71e5c7"
            entity_id: "light.nahtisch_decke"
          - name: "Energie Nähtisch Wandlampe"
            unique_id: "aade0a460235472ab3716e1e3ce18b0c"
            entity_id: "light.nahtisch_wand"
          - name: "Energie Steckdose Büro Ecke"
            unique_id: "5d867c6661f7420dab97e6ddfcb1efd2"
            entity_id: "switch.shelly_1pm_buero_ecke"
            power_sensor_id: "sensor.shelly_1pm_buero_ecke_power"
          - name: "Energie Steckdose Büro Tür"
            unique_id: "b6565ac585ff4b14b1b6f34a867586ae"
            entity_id: "switch.shelly_1pm_buero_tuer"
            power_sensor_id: "sensor.shelly_1pm_buero_tuer_power"
```

The two existing energy sensors contained in it are the enitiy_ids `switch.shelly_1pm_buero_ecke` and `sensor.shelly_1pm_buero_tuer_power`.

These are ESP Home devices that also provide an daily energy meter for via the `total_daily_energy` platform. When I look at them, it seems that the negative values are generated at the same time when the energy meter for the daily values resets (00:00 UTC, 01:00 CET):
![Screenshot 2023-03-02 205259](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7945681/222540851-36cc4a93-cbe6-49a3-a7ad-aa696fea9d32.png)

However, when I look at the energy meters generated by powercal for the yearly values, there are no anomalies to be seen either for the indivual lamps or for the two ESP energy meters in the group.

### Reproduction steps

1. Add a ESP Home Power Meter to a Powercalc Group
2. Add that Powercalc Group to the Energy Dashboard
3. Wait till midnight (UTC) to see if it produces negative values

body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have filled out the template to the best of my ability.
- [X] This only contains 1 feature request (if you have multiple feature requests, open one feature request for each feature request).
- [X] This issue is not a duplicate feature request of [previous feature requests](https://github.com/bramstroker/homeassistant-powercalc/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3A%22enhancement%22+).

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

As a follow up on #1544, it would be nice if there was a possibility to use an ´uncalibrated´ power plug such as the Blitzwolf SHP-13, and give it a percentual & fixed offset on their measured power value without using a template. From this new value, energy and utility sensors can be calculated.

For example:
```
{{ ((float(states('sensor.XXXX_power_uncalibrated'))
  * (float(100 - 3.29) / 100))
  + 1.3)
}}
```

Using 16 power plugs , all Blitzwolf SHP-13 (aka TuYa TS0121 / TuYa TS011F), I've noticed that these plugs aren't really accurate.
They almost always have an offset, which seems to be more or less percentual. This has to be determined in a test bench with fixed loads (and one calibrated/accurate plug).

There is a possibility to add power plugs to the configuration, such as the Blitzwolf SHP6-15A. The source entity must be the switch itself, so there is no relation to the measured power to begin with. After that, there is no way to make a relation with the measured power of the plug itself.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/12884006/222562723-b0c3b821-e456-44b5-ba30-ccb161091dfe.png)





### Describe the solution you'd like

I think a new configuration flow (or an edit of the existing one) needs to be made in order to support these kind of plugs, using the ideas described aboe.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

Current alternative is the power template. This doesn't work flawless and is slightly complicated.
An other alternative would be to use template in HA.

### Additional context

I might overlooked something in the documentation on how to use power plugs. If so, please point me to the right use of them.

This addon is for Home Assistant.

As a result it can't be run within the home-assistant most used hardware.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Docker measure support for arm64 which is Raspberry pi latest' platform.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

Running python on another computer and messing up with dependencies, environments, and discrepancies which is just too much.

### Additional context

Because HA already exposes ways to create Addons (which are HA-compatible docker containers), this could potentially help to do such migration to a HA-addonn-baseline image so that it runs in all supported HA platforms.

Nice to have: measure reelased as an HA addon (with environment variables defined through addon config) would greatly help on getting more calculations done from more users.

Thanks!

### Describe the issue

The FritzBox Integration https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/fritz has a feature of adding a switch to entities in the network, to enable or disable their internet access. On devices that are not supported by powercalc this is no problem as this switch is ignored.

However on devices (like a Shelly plug S) that are supported it seems to discover this as an extra relay and discovers a second powercalc sensor for it.

Im not a developer but not for home assistant so take the following with a grain of salt:
According to https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/ an entity has a property _entity_category_ which can be set to _config_ or _diagnostic_
I think an easy fix would be exclude entities with a _entity_category_ set to _config_ or _diagnostic_ in the powercalc discovery.


### Reproduction steps

1. use FritzBox Integration
2. use a device that is supported by powercalc and FritzBox Integration like a shelly Plug S
3. get discovery messages for the internet access switch

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Hello. Thank you for your software. This is proposal to make it even better!! :)

I just installed your software and it asks for Lifx LED strip (Lightstrip) "sub profile", where i can choose between 1 and 10. The only thing i get in mind is that this is active "zones" or maybe meters? Anyways i'm stuck, because i bought 3 meters, and cut it at about 2,70m. And this strip now have 21 zone. So should i put 3 (as closest by length) or this "sub profile" is zone count? 

### Describe the solution you'd like

It would be nice to have more precise setting, and more understandable. Are you talking about zones or meters? :) As the max sub profile value is 10, i believe this is in meters. The you should name it "meters" not "sub profile".

### Describe alternatives you've considered

As this item can by cut by length depending on the interior used. I see need to have zones, not meters. 
Please add possibility to choose by zones. 

It is not allow/possible to cut this led strip in the middle of the zone. You can cut only between zones. And in the app it shows how many zones it uses. So probably the best way to make accurate setting is by number of zones in the led. Please see print screen from app. 
![lifx_led_strip](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35271080/225666081-b05d5ee0-ef0d-46dd-8507-c7089ab1641e.jpg)


### Additional context

thank you!

### Checklist

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

I don't have a way to get readouts out of my gas meter, but I do have an entity that monitors if heating is on. Gas consumption is linear, as it would be in a light bulb. Only the unit "m³" doesn't match the unit kWh currently exclusively being used in powercalc.

### Describe the solution you'd like

It would be nice to be able to use a different unit than kWh, for example m³ for gas consumption.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

Alternatives would include creating it manually with a template sensor in YAML, but that's what powecalc is supposed to avoid doing. 

### Additional context

It would be nice to have gas consumption in the energy dashboard, in some cases this might be the only way.

### Describe the issue

I'm migrating my configuration from yaml to GUI. I'm using manual calibration for a few lights.

Here is my working yaml configuration (it's copy pasted from a group):
```
      - entity_id: light.0xec1bbdfffed8d9fe
        linear:
          calibrate:
            - 1 -> 0.2
            - 26 -> 0.3
            - 51 -> 0.3
            - 77 -> 0.4
            - 102 -> 0.5
            - 128 -> 0.6
            - 153 -> 0.8
            - 179 -> 1
            - 204 -> 1.3
            - 230 -> 1.8
            - 255 -> 2.4
        standby_power: 0.1
```

However, when I try to add the linear calibration via GUI, it doesn't work and relevant entities are not created.

Here is how I add the values:
![powercalc_1](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5116915/226745464-ffe301fc-2de5-41fc-9463-7d83885ba52f.png)

Here is how it looks when I configure the powercalc integration entity again:
![powercalc_2](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5116915/226745618-093302df-0a17-48c4-a081-904893f69119.png)

I read the documentation multiple times, so please let me know if I do something wrong. Thanks!

### Reproduction steps

1. Create Powercal integration, type: Virtual power (manual) using GUI
2. Select Calculation strategy: linear
3. Paste values as specified bellow the Calibration values field
4. Integration is created but entities are not

I also created a Powercalc sensor for the total of all rooms (to compare against actual house consumption to see my device monitoring gap) However, that total sensor does not even come close to the sum of all rooms together when looking at Energy. For Power it seems to work fine.

If you look at the properties of the total sensor it lists it's underlying 75 actual sensors (both PowerCalc Lights and PowerCalc Plugs device and actual PowerPlug consumptions). All individual sensos have a valid value, but the Total produced seems only a small part of it (0.07 kWh of 8.2 kWh as the sum of all the room usage and 8.6 kWh actual house consumption on the meter). 

I also have the general option active to ignore undefined/unknown states (and none of the detail devices has an unknown energy state)

How is this possible? Is there a limit in devices it can sum (it expands all aggregated groups correctly to the total list of actual detail devices to sum, it just doesn't doing the sum correctly).

* Take device, status (on/off) and program (P1, P2, etc) as input

  * for P1/P2/etc.: Define time dependent power consumptions, e.g. (0s -> 1kW; 600s -> 0.1kW; 3600s -> 0.001kW); Interpolation to be defined between points, e.g. constant, linear, etc.

Fully advanced solution: read the time dependent power consumption from a power plug and generate the values automatically.

By a plug for every appliance, but too expensive

body:
Currently include will include and create power sensors for all entities which are supported in powercalc library.

In v1.8.0 no powercalc entities are made magically anymore.

The user can setup a powercalc sensor using 3 methods:
- GUI discovery
- GUI manual
- YAML

`include` should only include powercalc entities which are explicitely defined using one of the above options.

Also have a look if we can include manually configured sensors (using the GUI) to the group.

            idle: 2
            error: 0
            cleaning: 0
            charging: 40

### Describe alternatives you've considered

The states can be extracted into separate entities and each can have a separate fixed power calc that is later merged into one number, but this approach is messy.

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Adding device power manually is annoying, i like the auto discovery! Smart cameras are a common device and take power, can we make profiles for their usage?

### Describe the solution you'd like

I would like to have the Power usage auto discovered for smart cameras, I have two Tapo cameras and I would like to add there power usage to may home assistant instance. 

### Describe alternatives you've considered

They could be added via custom power calculations, but it be nice to have them auto discovered and to be able to share power usage with the community 

### Additional context

I don't know how to best measure a camera since there are various operations some can do (like pan and tilt, night/day mode, etc, speaks etc. ). But I would at least like to have the base line power usage

### Describe the issue

On Powercalc 1.6.8, i have both configuration and Sensor Setup in configuration.yaml, and running totally **[See Section 1 on Diagnostics dump or YAML config].**

After Updating to Powercalc 1.8.4, with the needed restructuring of the Sensors-Entries, i decided to move everything with powercalc to a seperate file. configuration.yaml has only the Line `powercalc: !include powercalc.yaml`, and powercalc.yaml is restructured **[See Section 2 on Diagnostics dump or YAML config]**.

This throws out the Error after Restart **[See Debug logs]**.
```
Error during setup of component powercalc
(...)
TypeError: '<' not supported between instances of 'NodeDictClass' and 'NodeDictClass'
```

Narrowing down what might be a Problem, i found out that:
- ONE Sensor doesn't generate that Error, it seems to be fine
- It doesn't matter which one of the Sensors i go for, as long as it is one Sensor, it is fine
- TWO or more Sensors always lead to that Error
- It happens with-, and without Newlines between the Sensors

- When set the powercalc.yaml in such a (looks wrong to me) structure, it doesn't generate that Error. But then, when looking at those Sensors, they all are "unavailable", and it is said that they no longer are in use. Probably worthless, probably notable anyway.
```
sensors:
  - yyyyyy
sensors:
  - xxxxxxx
sensors:
  - zzzzzzz
```

Note: After i had to restore my Productional System twice, i changed to the dev-System (same Platform as well), but several Services not connected. That shouldn't make any difference, since the Error first happend with everything connected. Just to explain a couple of Errors in the Debug Log.

### Reproduction steps

1. Update Powercalc from 1.6.8 to 1.8.4
2. Move your Configuration and Sensors from configuration.yaml to powercalc.yaml, adopt the new Structure (See below)
3. Set up configuration.yaml to only use `powercalc: !include powercalc.yaml`

I have a "Tasmota-branded" Nous A1T Smart Plug which isn't properly recognised by the powercalc autodiscovery. I've enabled debug logging and discovered the following printout:

> 2023-08-15 21:23:57.610 DEBUG (MainThread) [custom_components.powercalc.discovery] switch.ender3v2: Auto discovered model (manufacturer=Tasmota, model=NOUS A1T)
> 2023-08-15 21:23:57.610 DEBUG (MainThread) [custom_components.powercalc.discovery] switch.ender3v2: Model not found in library, skipping discovery

For reference, the "Information" page of my Nous A1T shows the following info:
![image](https://github.com/bramstroker/homeassistant-powercalc/assets/3091695/8ecd2464-a1e7-42fe-9291-9226c1008d13)
![image](https://github.com/bramstroker/homeassistant-powercalc/assets/3091695/649bc026-d8f0-4f59-a11d-a2f3335d9920)


The manufacturer is listed as "Tasmota" and the model as "NOUS A1T". In #1721, support for Nous A1T was added, but this refers to manufacturer "Nous" and model "A1T". Within this PR, I have therefore added the required aliases to the manufacturer alias list as well as the device alias list. I can confirm that my Nous A1T plug gets discovered by powercalc using these settings.

**Note:** I am not entirely sure that adding the manufacturer alias is a good idea since it'll map **all** devices that report as being manufactured by "Tasmota" onto the "Nous" manufacturer. I am open to alternative solutions.

### Describe the issue

Hello,
I noticed that the entity "sensor.all_standby_energy" created by Powercalc never resets the sum.
I have reset Powercalc and all current measuring entities because of an error in the Energy Dashboard, deleted the db`s, reinstalled Powercalc and the sensor "sensor.all_standby_energy" still shows the sum from before....
In the statistics for the sensor there are also no entries that could be adjusted manually. The value is simply there.
I have configured even extra no devices in Powercalc, so the value can therefore not come...
Have now set the sensor once manually to 0. However, it is directly back to the old value....
![image](https://github.com/bramstroker/homeassistant-powercalc/assets/64659197/5d8c0eab-0af1-40f6-aa58-4e3b482c8e9a)
![image](https://github.com/bramstroker/homeassistant-powercalc/assets/64659197/1df781f4-8184-4bff-a3ea-b7e47fa1603f)
![image](https://github.com/bramstroker/homeassistant-powercalc/assets/64659197/4ba1b86a-6752-4590-98f3-6a7195d528fd)


### Reproduction steps

1. uninstall Powercalc
2. delete all db
3. delete Powecalc entity "All standby energy"
4. restart HA
5. reinstall Powercalc without configuring devices
6. all standby energy entity back with old values.

title: Improve hass controller support with self-signed ssl certificates in powercalc-measure
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have filled out the template to the best of my ability.
- [X] This only contains 1 feature request (if you have multiple feature requests, open one feature request for each feature request).
- [X] This issue is not a duplicate feature request of [previous feature requests](https://github.com/bramstroker/homeassistant-powercalc/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3A%22enhancement%22+).

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

### Background story
I would like to contribute measured data for some lights currently unsupported by powercalc. For that purpose I tried using the powercalc-measure docker image from within my Manjaro Linux system. Initially I failed (understandably) to connect to my Home-Assistant which I set up as the light and power sensor controller (within the powercalc-measure `.env` file). Reason: certificate could not be verified.
My Home-Assistant is configured to use https, only. Its using a certificate signed by my own root certificate authority.
### First tries
I have a root certificate (a .pem file) installed to `/etc/ca-certificates/extracted/` ([further info](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/User:Grawity/Adding_a_trusted_CA_certificate)). Initially I tried to map the `/etc/ssl` and `/etc/ca-certificates` as docker volumes but without any success. Python does not seem to consider these system default paths while `wget 'https://HA-HOST'` works fine.
I found out that there is an environment variable `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` used by Python. It should point to the certificate file to be used for SSL verification.
### Solution that works fine for me
I created a bash script to run the docker:
```
#!/bin/bash
set -e

SCRIPT_DIR="$(dirname -- "${0}")"

mkdir -p -- "${SCRIPT_DIR}/export"
mkdir -p -- "${SCRIPT_DIR}/.persistent"
docker run \
    --rm --name=powercalc-measure \
    --env-file="${SCRIPT_DIR}/.env" \
    -e REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE=/app/hass_cert.pem \
    -v /etc/ca-certificates/extracted/cadir/myca.pem:/app/hass_cert.pem \
    -v "${SCRIPT_DIR}/export:/app/export" \
    -v "${SCRIPT_DIR}/.persistent:/app/.persistent" \
    -it bramgerritsen/powercalc-measure:latest
```

### Describe the solution you'd like

Update the documentation and add a new environment variable in the `.env` file that can hold the path or the content of a certificate to help new users setup hass as the controller for contributing measurement data.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

Update the documentation, only.

### Additional context

N/A

### Describe the issue

In the logs an error is logged with `create_group`: 

``` sensor.electric_heating_auxiliary: Skipping sensor setup: Cannot select a strategy (LINEAR, FIXED or LUT, WLED), supply it in the config. See the readme ```

The definition of `sensor.electric_heating_auxiliary` is the following:

```
powercalc:
  sensors:
    - create_group: electric_heating_auxiliary
      entities:
        - power_sensor_id: sensor.system_wtw_metering_plug_verwarming_power
          energy_sensor_id: sensor.system_wtw_metering_plug_verwarming_energy
        - power_sensor_id: sensor.floor0_living_metering_plug_verwarming_power
          energy_sensor_id: sensor.floor0_living_metering_plug_verwarming_energy
```

both `system_wtw_metering_plug_verwarming` and `floor0_living_metering_plug_verwarming` are a metering plug, so no powercalc sensors. 

I believe the error is thus incorrect.

1. Configure create_group powercalc sensor as specified

### Describe the issue

Powercalc groups unexpected do not respect the "Ignore unavailable state" of group items until first seen by Home-Assistant.

### Reproduction steps

1. Add a Powercalc sensor for a device which is currently unavailable (powered off).
2. Configure the just added Powercalc to "Ignore unavailable state" (set switch to enabled) and set the "Unavailable power" to "0".
3. Verify that the just added Powercalc "power" sensor indeed shows 0 Watts.
4. Create a Powercalc group containing that initially added Powercalc sensor.
5. **The Powercalc group's power sensor does not show 0 Watts as expected but "Unknown".**
6. Power the device and make sure it's available to HA. The Powercalc group's power sensor starts showing the expected value.
7. Unpower the device or make sure its state is "unavailable". The Powercalc group's power sensor continues to show 0 Watt value as expected.
8. **Restart Home-Assistant while the device is unpowered. The Powercalc group's power sensor again shows "Unknown" instead of 0 watts.**

body: @bramstroker Am I right that Utility meters (daily, weekly, monthly) are not able to run backwards, but only collect instead? e.g. If I do a Riemann of a powermeter, and there will be a short time of 'negative' power, like so: the Powercalc version does this: (same source) In this case (heat pump) things like start-up, or defrosting of the heat pump, causing a reverse thermal power, are not taken into account. Not only does it not reverse calculation, it doesn't even pause during the time the power reverses.

body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have filled out the template to the best of my ability.
- [X] This only contains 1 feature request (if you have multiple feature requests, open one feature request for each feature request).
- [X] This issue is not a duplicate feature request of [previous feature requests](https://github.com/bramstroker/homeassistant-powercalc/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3A%22enhancement%22+).

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

My feature request is based on the need to make the calculated values from Powercalc available in other systems such as InfluxDB or via MQTT. This enables advanced data storage and analysis, without to have all Sensors in Homeassistant.

### Describe the solution you'd like

I propose adding a feature to integrate Powercalc with InfluxDB and optionally with MQTT in Home Assistant. Here are the details:

InfluxDB Integration (Preferred Solution): Add a configuration option that allows the calculated values from Powercalc to be written directly to an InfluxDB database. Users should configure their InfluxDB connection details and the corresponding database.

Example configuration in configuration.yaml:

```yaml
powercalc:
  influxdb:
    host: influxdb_host
    port: influxdb_port
    database: influxdb_database
    username: influxdb_username
    password: influxdb_password
```
### Describe alternatives you've considered

MQTT Integration (Alternative Solution): Optionally, users could also publish the calculated values from Powercalc via MQTT. Users should be able to configure the MQTT broker details and the desired topic.

Example configuration in configuration.yaml:

```yaml
powercalc:
  mqtt:
    broker: mqtt_broker
    port: mqtt_port
    topic: mqtt_topic
```
### Additional context

Integrating Powercalc with InfluxDB would allow users to seamlessly use energy consumption information in other applications, such as Grafana for data visualization or custom scripts for advanced analysis. The alternative solution via MQTT remains an option for users who prefer this integration or already use an existing MQTT system. This would enhance the flexibility of Home Assistant and facilitate integration into existing IoT ecosystems.

title: aliases for devices
body:
**First of all: Happy New Year!
And also THANK YOU for the time you invest in the project.**

I'm not sure if the following pull request is the best solution. However, I do see a problem with the topic and would like to suggest this as a possible solution. I'm sure you can think of better solutions :-)

Problem: Shelly Plug S is now in tasmota and shelly-data-folder as well (Thanks for merging my commits 👍 ).
But: discovery doesn't work. 
Cause: Tasmota is an manufactor alias for "nous" (set in aliases.py).

One Solution might be: copy "shelly plus s" configs to nous as well. But then in the HA UI it will be shown "nous shelly plug s" instead of "tasmota shelly plug s" which is okay, but is confusing.

Therefore, a mechanism might be needed where not only manufacturers get an alias, but also individual devices.
Since nous, for example, apparently does not sell all devices with tasmota, this would also make sense for other OEMs as well.

This would work with code changes and e.g. extensions to model.json schema. 
But it also works at file level with symlinks - that would be the pull request.

As I said, I'm not sure if this is the best way or if it should rather be solved in code.
So please understand this as a suggestion only.


On the filesystem is looks like that:
```
# the files 
dxr-xr-x    nous
drwxr-xr-x    nous/A1Z
-rw-r--r--    nous/A1Z/model.json
drwxr-xr-x    nous/A1T
-rw-r--r--    nous/A1T/model.json
drwxr-xr-x    shelly
drwxr-xr-x    shelly/shelly plus plug s
-rw-r--r--    shelly/shelly plus plug s/model.json
drwxr-xr-x    shelly/shelly plug s
-rw-r--r--    shelly/shelly plug s/model.json
# the alias via links for devices flashed with tasmota
drwxr-xr-x    tasmota
lrwxrwxrwx    tasmota/A1Z -> ../nous/A1Z
lrwxrwxrwx    tasmota/A1T -> ../nous/A1T
lrwxrwxrwx    tasmota/shelly plug s -> ../shelly/shelly plug s
lrwxrwxrwx    tasmota/shelly plus plug s -> ../shelly/shelly plus plug s
```
