-   [`unnecessary-dict-comprehension-for-iterable`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/unnecessary-dict-comprehension-for-iterable/): `RUF025` to `C420`

##### Stabilization

The following rules have been stabilized and are no longer in preview:

-   [`singledispatch-method`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/singledispatch-method/) (`PLE1519`)
-   [`singledispatchmethod-function`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/singledispatchmethod-function/) (`PLE1520`)
-   [`bad-staticmethod-argument`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/bad-staticmethod-argument/) (`PLW0211`)
-   [`if-stmt-min-max`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/if-stmt-min-max/) (`PLR1730`)
-   [`invalid-bytes-return-type`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/invalid-bytes-return-type/) (`PLE0308`)
-   [`invalid-hash-return-type`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/invalid-hash-return-type/) (`PLE0309`)
-   [`invalid-index-return-type`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/invalid-index-return-type/) (`PLE0305`)
-   [`invalid-length-return-type`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/invalid-length-return-type/) (`E303`)
-   [`self-or-cls-assignment`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/self-or-cls-assignment/) (`PLW0642`)
-   [`byte-string-usage`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/byte-string-usage/) (`PYI057`)
-   [`duplicate-literal-member`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/duplicate-literal-member/) (`PYI062`)
-   [`redirected-noqa`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/redirected-noqa/) (`RUF101`)

The following behaviors have been stabilized:

-   [`cancel-scope-no-checkpoint`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/cancel-scope-no-checkpoint/) (`ASYNC100`): Support `asyncio` and `anyio` context mangers.
-   [`async-function-with-timeout`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/async-function-with-timeout/) (`ASYNC109`): Support `asyncio` and `anyio` context mangers.
-   [`async-busy-wait`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/async-busy-wait/) (`ASYNC110`): Support `asyncio` and `anyio` context mangers.
-   [`async-zero-sleep`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/async-zero-sleep/) (`ASYNC115`): Support `anyio` context mangers.
-   [`long-sleep-not-forever`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/long-sleep-not-forever/) (`ASYNC116`): Support `anyio` context mangers.

The following fixes have been stabilized:

-   [`superfluous-else-return`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/superfluous-else-return/) (`RET505`)
-   [`superfluous-else-raise`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/superfluous-else-raise/) (`RET506`)
-   [`superfluous-else-continue`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/superfluous-else-continue/) (`RET507`)
-   [`superfluous-else-break`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/superfluous-else-break/) (`RET508`)

##### Preview features

-   \[`flake8-simplify`] Further simplify to binary in preview for (`SIM108`) ([#​12796](https://togithub.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/12796))
-   \[`pyupgrade`] Show violations without auto-fix (`UP031`) ([#​11229](https://togithub.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/11229))

##### Rule changes

-   \[`flake8-import-conventions`] Add `xml.etree.ElementTree` to default conventions ([#​12455](https://togithub.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/12455))
-   \[`flake8-pytest-style`] Add a space after comma in CSV output (`PT006`) ([#​12853](https://togithub.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/12853))

##### Server

-   Show a message for incorrect settings ([#​12781](https://togithub.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/12781))

##### Bug fixes

-   \[`flake8-async`] Do not lint yield in context manager (`ASYNC100`) ([#​12896](https://togithub.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/12896))
-   \[`flake8-comprehensions`] Do not lint `async for` comprehensions (`C419`) ([#​12895](https://togithub.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/12895))
-   \[`flake8-return`] Only add return `None` at end of a function (`RET503`) ([#​11074](https://togithub.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/11074))
-   \[`flake8-type-checking`] Avoid treating `dataclasses.KW_ONLY` as typing-only (`TCH003`) ([#​12863](https://togithub.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/12863))
-   \[`pep8-naming`] Treat `type(Protocol)` et al as metaclass base (`N805`) ([#​12770](https://togithub.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/12770))
-   \[`pydoclint`] Don't enforce returns and yields in abstract methods (`DOC201`, `DOC202`) ([#​12771](https://togithub.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/12771))
-   \[`ruff`] Skip tuples with slice expressions in (`RUF031`) ([#​12768](https://togithub.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/12768))
-   \[`ruff`] Ignore unparenthesized tuples in subscripts when the subscript is a type annotation or type alias (`RUF031`) ([#​12762](https://togithub.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/12762))
-   \[`ruff`] Ignore template strings passed to logging and `builtins._()` calls (`RUF027`) ([#​12889](https://togithub.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/12889))
-   \[`ruff`] Do not remove parens for tuples with starred expressions in Python <=3.10 (`RUF031`) ([#​12784](https://togithub.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/12784))
-   Evaluate default parameter values for a function in that function's enclosing scope ([#​12852](https://togithub.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/12852))

##### Other changes

-   Respect `kernelspec` notebook metadata when detecting the preferred language for a Jupyter Notebook ([#​12875](https://togithub.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/12875))

- [x] This issue is not a duplicate issue of currently [previous issues](https://github.com/bramstroker/homeassistant-powercalc/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3A%22bug%22+)..

### Describe the issue

Powercalc version 1.14.0, after updating Home Assistant to version 2024.8.0, is unable to operate group-type entities. The already created entity all_standby_power is functioning, but the entity all_standby_energy shows as 'unknown'. The same issue occurs with a created group that contains all data managed by powercalc. The sensor's name is sensor.powercalc_all_energy, while its state is 'Unavailable'. On the other hand, sensor.powercalc_all_power is working correctly. The problem is clearly confined to groups and energy-type entities.

I tried removing powercalc and recreating the groups, running it on a new instance, but nothing worked. I also tried removing some entities from the group that contains sensor.powercalc_all_energy to see if it would work, but nothing changed. The only slightly unusual configuration I made with powercalc was manually deleting the core.restore_state file to reset the values because resetting the various sensors using the utility provided by powercalc resulted in negative values.

### Reproduction steps

1. Install Powercalc from HACS and restart.
2. Add powercalc: to the configuration files and restart.
3. Configure some entities from the Home Assistant dashboard using powercalc manual mode and others using powercalc virtual mode.
4. Create an entity using the standard group mode.
5. Wait a few days to verify that everything is working.
6. Try resetting the sensor with `powercalc.reset_energy` and check that all values are negative, attempting to calibrate them without success.
7. Stop the Home Assistant instance, delete MariaDB and `core.restore_state`, restart, and finally have the values reset.
8. Update Home Assistant to version 2024.8.0 and enjoy that no energy-type groups work.

### Describe the issue

Installed the integration, set
```
powercalc:
  enable_autodiscovery: true
```
in the YAML and restarted HA.

Did not yet try to add the integration via the UI.

HA log now contains errors:

```
Logger: homeassistant.config_entries
Quelle: config_entries.py:2444
Erstmals aufgetreten: 15:49:37 (17 Vorkommnisse)
Zuletzt protokolliert: 15:56:13

Error occurred loading flow for integration powercalc: cannot import name 'ConfigEntryBaseFlow' from 'homeassistant.config_entries' (/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/config_entries.py)
```

Trying to add it via the UI once this is shown (and above LOG error event is increased +1):
![grafik](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/eb576b8b-5dd0-4f65-a1bb-4248c291c0c5)

Maybe the integration (v1.14.2) does not match HA Core version? Even the installed 2024.3.3 matches the required 2024.3.0 in https://github.com/bramstroker/homeassistant-powercalc/blob/master/hacs.json.

##### NumPy 2.1.1 Release Notes

NumPy 2.1.1 is a maintenance release that fixes bugs and regressions
discovered after the 2.1.0 release.

The Python versions supported by this release are 3.10-3.13.

##### Contributors

A total of 7 people contributed to this release. People with a "+" by
their names contributed a patch for the first time.

-   Andrew Nelson
-   Charles Harris
-   Mateusz Sokół
-   Maximilian Weigand +
-   Nathan Goldbaum
-   Pieter Eendebak
-   Sebastian Berg

##### Pull requests merged

A total of 10 pull requests were merged for this release.

-   [#​27236](https://redirect.github.com/numpy/numpy/pull/27236): REL: Prepare for the NumPy 2.1.0 release \[wheel build]
-   [#​27252](https://redirect.github.com/numpy/numpy/pull/27252): MAINT: prepare 2.1.x for further development
-   [#​27259](https://redirect.github.com/numpy/numpy/pull/27259): BUG: revert unintended change in the return value of set_printoptions
-   [#​27266](https://redirect.github.com/numpy/numpy/pull/27266): BUG: fix reference counting bug in \__array_interface\_\_ implementation...
-   [#​27267](https://redirect.github.com/numpy/numpy/pull/27267): TST: Add regression test for missing descr in array-interface
-   [#​27276](https://redirect.github.com/numpy/numpy/pull/27276): BUG: Fix [#​27256](https://redirect.github.com/numpy/numpy/issues/27256) and [#​27257](https://redirect.github.com/numpy/numpy/issues/27257)
-   [#​27278](https://redirect.github.com/numpy/numpy/pull/27278): BUG: Fix array_equal for numeric and non-numeric scalar types
-   [#​27287](https://redirect.github.com/numpy/numpy/pull/27287): MAINT: Update maintenance/2.1.x after the 2.0.2 release

title: Model Schema adding general description
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have filled out the template to the best of my ability.
- [X] This only contains 1 feature request (if you have multiple feature requests, open one feature request for each feature request).
- [X] This issue is not a duplicate feature request of [previous feature requests](https://github.com/bramstroker/homeassistant-powercalc/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3A%22enhancement%22+).

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Devices are numerous and are sometimes difficult to differentiate. Additionally sometimes the models in the library can have special settings or purposes.

### Describe the solution you'd like

It would be great to have an additional property to be able to generally describe the device, the model and other. Hence, it would be great to add the property "description" or less perfect "device_description" to the model schema

### Describe alternatives you've considered

I considered to add comments but json does natively not support comments. There are parsers that do but this is not a native feature to json afk.

### Additional context

none

title: Document hardware suggestions for measurements (power plugs etc. and resistive loads)
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have filled out the template to the best of my ability.
- [x] This only contains 1 feature request (if you have multiple feature requests, open one feature request for each feature request).
- [x] This issue is not a duplicate feature request of [previous feature requests](https://github.com/bramstroker/homeassistant-powercalc/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3A%22enhancement%22+).

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

As noticed in https://github.com/bramstroker/homeassistant-powercalc/discussions/4488#discussioncomment-17953640 the documentation is great on the software side, but for good measurements also the hardware is important. And (especially for non-electotechnicians and noobs like me) the docs are missing that, currently. 

### Describe the solution you'd like

* first of all, document and suggest for power plugs or so that may be used for measuring
  * if know, the measure accuracy would be good to know
  * same for the minimum load it can measure 
* then, the resistive loads
  * what it is in general and why
  * which is recommend and why
  * alternatives
  * how to get them (see discussion linked above)

### Describe alternatives you've considered

None, documentation is important for newbies especially

Users may also be guided in the app itself, but IMHO, for this more complex topic, this may just be links to the relevant docs. 

### Additional context

N/A

title: Add dreame dreame.vacuum.r2205 power profile
body:
## Description

This PR updates the existing `RLS3D` profile (Dreame D10 Plus) with a new, complete measurement run and addresses the review feedback.

> **This is a replacement of the existing `RLS3D` profile, not a new profile.** The model id `dreame.vacuum.r2205` and the legacy id `d10-plus` are kept, so existing installations and discovery keep working.

### Device information
- **Manufacturer**: Dreame
- **Model ID**: `dreame.vacuum.r2205`
- **Product name**: D10 Plus
- **Measurement device**: Shelly Plug S Gen3
- **Measurement method**: Powercalc Measure (recorder), `dreame_vacuum` integration
- **Mains voltage during recording**: ~229 V

### Recording coverage
- **4.66 h run** — full clean from 99 % down to 34 %, then the charge back to 100 % (8,083 samples, ~2 s interval)
- **Two dock-only runs** of ~2 minutes each at 100 %, used to confirm the settled docked level

All values are time averages over the window in which the matching condition holds, not peak values.

### What changed in the profile

**Metadata restored.** The previous revision had an empty `name` and had dropped `aliases`, `legacy_ids`, `compatible_integrations`, `product_url` and `device_specs`. All of them are back, so discovery and migration stay intact.

**Sleeping branch corrected.** The previous revision returned a flat 8.14 W for the sleeping state. The recordings show 2.36 W once the station has settled, confirmed by all three runs (2.36 W, 2.36 W, 2.42 W).

**Charging covers the full battery range.** The new run only covers 35–99 %. For 16–34 % the values from the previous recording of the same device are carried over unchanged, since that range is correct and was not re-measured. Both runs agree in their overlapping range 35–39 % within 0.2 W (the new values are 0.12–0.16 W higher). The old 15 % point (17.31 W) was **not** carried over, because it captures the charging ramp-in rather than the steady level; below 16 % the 16 % value is used as a flat estimate.

**Auto-empty averaged over the whole active interval.** `auto_empty_status` is active for only about 8–13 s per cycle. The plateau inside that window is 668 W on the long run and 653 W on the dock-only runs, but its first 4–6 s are still at dock level (2–21 W) and one intermediate sample of 198–242 W was captured. The profile uses **400 W**, the average over the complete active interval (33 samples, mean 399.8 W), which is exactly the interval the condition spans — so the ramp-up is included instead of being reported as a peak.

**`measure_description` filled in** with coverage and the remaining limitations (see below).

### Remaining limitations (documented in `model.json`)

- **The first 31 minutes after a charge are not modelled separately.** Directly after charging finishes the station still draws 14.9 W and decays to about 2.4 W over roughly 31 minutes (measured: 4.47 Wh in that window). The profile reports the settled 2.36 W there instead, so each completed charge is under-counted by about **3.25 Wh**.
  Modelling the decay would need a time-based template on `charging_state.last_changed`, which restarts on every Home Assistant restart or unavailable→off transition of that entity and would then *overstate* power for a full window. The settled value is used on purpose instead of reintroducing a timer.
- **The 100 % transition is not distinguished** for the same reason. `charging_state` drops while the robot still reports `charging` (about 15.0 W for ~10 s after a full charge, but only 2.4–2.8 W on a settled dock). That window falls into the docked branch.
- **Charging below 16 %** is a flat extrapolation and not measured.
- **Two samples** in the long run show an auto-empty while `auto_empty_status` still reports `idle` (651 W). That combination is not modelled and falls through to the docked branch.

### Validation

The profile was replayed against all three recordings (8,212 samples):

| Branch | Samples | Measured | Predicted | MAE |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| away from dock | 1,911 | 0.45 W | 0.45 W | 0.06 W |
| charging | 5,214 | 21.80 W | 21.56 W | 0.41 W |
| docked / sleeping | 1,054 | 9.03 W | 2.36 W | 6.67 W |
| auto-empty | 33 | 399.76 W | 400 W | 303.98 W |
| **total** | **8,212** | | | **2.35 W** |

The high auto-empty MAE is inherent to modelling an 8–13 s ramp as a single average; per sample it is large, but integrated over all three recordings the branch matches almost exactly (7.56 Wh measured against 7.57 Wh modelled, difference below 0.01 Wh). The docked MAE comes from the intentionally unmodelled 31-minute decay described above.

**Whole-run energy**, over the complete long recording: measured **75.63 Wh**, predicted **71.15 Wh** — an underestimate of **5.9 %**. That gap is dominated by the unmodelled post-charge decay, which accounts for about 3.25 Wh per completed charge.

### Checklist
- [x] Single PR per device
- [x] Only the `model.json` of this profile is touched
- [x] Metadata (name, aliases, legacy ids, integrations, product url, specs) preserved
- [x] `measure_description` documents coverage and limitations
- [x] Generated and validated with Powercalc Measure
- [x] Schema validation against `profile_library/model_schema.json` passes
- [x] `min_version: v1.25.5` set, required for the per-strategy `entity_id` override used by the charging strategy

### Generated files
- `profile_library/dreame/RLS3D/model.json`

title: Normalize line endings of the Linkind profile CSVs
body:
## Problem

`.gitattributes` declares `profile_library/**/*.csv` as `text eol=lf`, but the two Linkind profile CSVs were committed with CRLF line endings:

```
profile_library/linkind/LS0125051883A/color_temp.csv   (2185 lines)
profile_library/linkind/LS0125051883A/hs.csv           (2026 lines)
```

Because the blobs in the repository violate their own attribute, `git update-index --refresh` reports both files as `needs update` on **every** fresh checkout, even though the working tree is clean.

## Impact

This breaks the `pre-commit` workflow for **unrelated** PRs. The `j178/prek-action` step itself passes all hooks; the failure comes from the downstream `pre-commit-ci/lite-action`, which uses `_has_changes()` to decide whether to push an auto-fix commit:

```
profile_library/linkind/LS0125051883A/color_temp.csv: needs update
profile_library/linkind/LS0125051883A/hs.csv: needs update
fetching pr...
error: Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by merge:
        profile_library/linkind/LS0125051883A/color_temp.csv
        profile_library/linkind/LS0125051883A/hs.csv
fatal: cherry-pick failed
```

The action sees a dirty tree that has nothing to do with the incoming PR, tries to cherry-pick its own fix commit onto it, and aborts. Contributors cannot get a green `pre-commit` check on a clean profile PR because of files they never touched.

## Reproduction

On a fresh checkout of `master`:

```text
git update-index --refresh        # exit 1, both files reported as "needs update"
```

With the fix applied:

```text
git update-index --refresh        # exit 0
```

## Fix

`git add --renormalize` on the two files. Content is unchanged — only the line endings differ:

```
color_temp.csv   HEAD md5 (CR stripped) = 6414724a91e0 …   after = 6414724a91e0 …   identical
hs.csv           HEAD md5 (CR stripped) = b7c3e8d3a1e4 …   after = b7c3e8d3a1e4 …   identical
```

Line counts are unchanged as well (2185 / 2026). The stored blobs are now `i/lf`, matching the attribute.

```
 profile_library/linkind/LS0125051883A/color_temp.csv | 4370 +++++++++---------
 profile_library/linkind/LS0125051883A/hs.csv         | 4052 ++++++++---------
 2 files changed, 4211 insertions(+), 4211 deletions(-)
```

## Scope

Only these two files are affected. `master` contains eleven other CRLF files (eight `shelly/S3SW-002P16EU/*/model.json`, three `tests/.../profiles/test/*.csv`), but none of them carry an `eol` attribute, so they do not trigger the bug and are deliberately left untouched.

No profile data, values or metadata change in this PR.

title: Battery-rate power strategy
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have filled out the template to the best of my ability.
- [x] This only contains 1 feature request (if you have multiple feature requests, open one feature request for each feature request).
- [x] This issue is not a duplicate feature request of [previous feature requests](https://github.com/bramstroker/homeassistant-powercalc/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3A%22enhancement%22+).

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Raised in my Saros 10R profile PR #5075 : This device sometimes uses a fast (40-50 W) or slow (~21 W) charge mode during charging with no discernible trigger/pattern and nothing in the Roborock entities indicate which mode is active. Using the normal a battery-% table will undercount fast-mode charges or over-count slow-mode charges.


### Describe the solution you'd like

A new strategy that derives power from battery charging rate: 

`power = base_power + max(0, d(battery %)/dt [%/h]) * energy_per_percent [Wh/%]`

For example, as a sub-strategy inside `composite`:
```json
{
  "condition": { "...": "status == charging" },
  "battery_rate": {
    "entity_id": "[[entity_by_device_class:battery]]",
    "energy_per_percent": 0.96,
    "base_power": 3.5,
    "window": 600,
    "max_power": 60
  }
}
```
- `base_power` covers the always-on part: the docked baseline or baseline + drying in a drying branch
- `window` is the smoothing window in seconds
- `max_power` clamps glitches, e.g. a battery reading that jumps several % at once

**What I run locally:**

1. Derivative helper on the battery sensor: `unit_time: h`, `time_window: 00:10:00`, `round: 1`, `max_sub_interval: 00:02:00`.
   - Note: Without `max_sub_interval`, the derivative holds its last value after the battery stops changing instead of decaying to 0.

2. A template sensor (washing/emptying branches omitted):
   ```jinja
   {% set rate = states('sensor.jarvis_battery_pct_per_hour') | float(0) %}
   {% set p = 3.5 %}                                    {# docked baseline #}
   {% if is_state('binary_sensor.jarvis_dock_mop_drying','on') %}{% set p = p + 57.2 %}{% endif %}
   {% if is_state('binary_sensor.jarvis_charging','on') and rate > 0 %}{% set p = p + rate * 0.96 %}{% endif %}
   {{ p | round(1) }}
   ```

**Validation.** Replayed against a ThirdReality plug's 1 Wh energy counter. The battery % rate is approximated as the change over the trailing 10 min, at 0.96 Wh/%:

| Charge window | Plug | Battery-rate | Battery-% table (profile from PR) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tue, fast ~10 min then slow, drying | 210 Wh | -0% | -3% |
| Wed, slow, drying | 260 Wh | +1% | +3% |
| Thu, slow, drying | 242 Wh | +0% | +0% |
| Fri, fast to 81%, drying | 198 Wh | +0% | -13% |
| Sat, slow, no drying | 96 Wh | +2% | +1% |
| Mon, fast mid-run recharge, no drying | 43 Wh | -1% | -43% |
| Mon, final charge, drying | 169 Wh | -2% | -5% |
| **Total** | **1218 Wh** | **+0.1%** | **-4.1%** |

- The above template running in HA for ~49 hrs (including full run and charge) came within +0.2% of the plug

### Describe alternatives you've considered

- Battery-% -> W table (`linear` on the battery entity): following slow mode (what #5075 uses). Comes within 0-3% on slow charges but -13% and -43% on fast-mode charges.

- Flat charging wattage: an energy-weighted average (26.5 W) across the measured charges came out right over the whole week but -28% to +13% per charge and it misses the taper above ~92%

- Separate fast/slow sub-profiles: The mode isn't exposed by the integration (can't know which is active) and it will change partway through a charge

- A template in the profile: templates only see the battery's current value, not its history, so a rate can't be computed

- A custom field asking the user for a derivative entity works in theory, but custom fields are required in the config flow so users would have to build the derivative helper *before* the profile could install



### Additional context

Also applies to any device with a battery % entity whose charger power varies (mowers or phones/tablets on smart chargers).

`energy_per_percent` will need a measured charge per model, like any other profile.


* [jarvis_charge_2026-10-24_clean.png](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/55aecfe9-c04e-4b3d-b32a-776924027de9): clean slow-mode charge
* [jarvis_charge_traces.png](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bee9802d-3605-4457-ba5c-14cfa89d0884): all charges overlaid against the merged table
* [jarvis_charge_raw_traces.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34155448/jarvis_charge_raw_traces.zip): per-charge CSVs (plug power, energy counter, battery %, status, drying)

body:
## What this adds

An optional second group that sums the power of the devices that are
currently switched on. It is **disabled by default** and does not change the
meaning of `sensor.all_standby_power`.

This PR is now scoped to the active group only. The independent parts were
split out on request:

- #5166 - group energy sensors keep their own name
- #5167 - `standby_power_on` as a sensor option
- #5168 - extract the group summation into a base class

## Why

`sensor.all_standby_power` shows phantom consumption: the standby power of
devices that are off plus the operating overhead of smart plugs, dimmers and
similar devices, even while their connected load is on. That is the
documented behaviour and it stays exactly as it is.

What is missing is the other half: a total of what the devices that are on
are using right now. Today that is only visible per device, and a device that
is switched on without a `standby_power_on` in its profile does not appear in
any total at all.

## Behaviour

- `create_active_group: false` (default) - no new entities, no change for
  existing installations
- `create_active_group: true` - adds
  - `sensor.all_self_usage_power` - power of the devices that are on
  - `sensor.all_self_usage_energy` - accumulated energy of those devices

A device takes part while it is switched on and contributes its actual power.
When it is switched off it leaves the group again. The standby group is not
touched in either case.

### Configuration

```yaml
powercalc:
  create_active_group: true
```

The option is also available in the global configuration flow, step
"Create sensors".

## Testing

- `pytest tests` -> 1589 passed, 1 skipped
- coverage gate passes (100%)
- 3 tests in `tests/test_discovery.py` fail in my environment and fail
  identically on the untouched base commit
- verified live on a Home Assistant instance: with the option enabled a lamp
  switched to 100 % shows 8.43 W in `all_self_usage_power` while
  `all_standby_power` stays unchanged

title: feat(standby): allow standby_power_on for manually configured sensors
body:
## Problem

Power profiles can declare the power a device draws for its own operation while it is switched on
(`standby_power_on`). A manually configured sensor could not express that value.

`_get_standby_power()` returned `(standby_power, 0)` as soon as `standby_power` was configured
directly, so the ON state value was always 0. This affects devices that are modelled by hand instead
of by a library profile - a router, a UPS, a NAS. While running they draw a bit more than their
standby value, and that difference was silently dropped.

## Change

`standby_power_on` is now accepted as a sensor option:

```yaml
powercalc:
  sensors:
    - entity_id: sensor.my_router
      mode: fixed
      fixed:
        power: 12.4
      standby_power: 12.4
      standby_power_on: 12.4   # power it draws while running
```

- it takes precedence over the value from a power profile
- without the option nothing changes, the behaviour is identical to before

## Testing

- `pytest tests/sensors/group/test_standby.py` -> 12 passed
- new test `test_standby_power_on_option` verifies the power sensor and the standby total for both
  states of a manually configured sensor
- coverage gate stays green (option and no-option path are both covered)

title: Add Dreame/Mova E30 Ultra (RLE51SE) power profile
body:
## Description

Adds a new composite power profile for the **Mova E30 Ultra** robot vacuum with self-emptying, mop-washing and drying base station. The device is sold under the Mova brand (a Dreame sister brand) and Home Assistant reports the model as `dreame.vacuum.r2427a`, so the profile is filed under `profile_library/dreame/` like the other Dreame vacuum profiles. The library has no separate `mova` directory. The directory uses the printed robot model `RLE51SE`; `dreame.vacuum.r2427a` stays as the discovery alias.

This is the follow-up to discussion #4650. The two earlier PRs for this device were closed because the profile was still preliminary (wrong `states_power` shape, then a hand-built composite with invalid `linear` options). It is a **new** profile, not a replacement.

### Device information
- **Manufacturer**: Mova (Home Assistant manufacturer: `Dreametech™`)
- **Model ID (discovery alias)**: `dreame.vacuum.r2427a`
- **Robot model**: `RLE51SE`
- **Dock model**: `RCEE0301`
- **Product name**: E30 Ultra
- **Integration**: `dreame_vacuum`
- **Firmware during recording**: `4.3.9_1539`
- **Measurement device**: Shelly Plug S Gen3, between the wall socket and the base station
- **Measurement method**: Powercalc Measure `v0.14.1` (recorder, vacuum recipe, ~2 s sample interval)
- **Mains voltage during recording**: ~230 V

The plug sits upstream of the whole station, so every value covers the station plus the robot while it is docked. While the robot cleans, it runs on battery and the station only draws standby power.

### Recording coverage
- **6.33 h run** — full clean from 100 % down to 15 %, mop washing and drying cycles, then a charge from 15 % to 99 %. The 18–73 % part of that charge ran while mop drying was active.
- **25.2 min run** — charge completion at 99–100 % and the first 13 minutes of the post-charge tail.
- **Two dock-only runs** of 3.1 min and 2.4 min at 100 %, used to confirm the settled docked level.
- **11,797 samples / 6.84 h in total.**

All values are time averages over the window in which the matching condition holds, not peak values.

### Branches

| Condition | Power | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `auto_empty_status = active` | **414.5 W** | 7 episodes of 6–17 s (47 samples, 98 s). Plateau 540–576 W, but the average over the complete active interval is 414.5 W, including the ramp-up. |
| `self_wash_base_status = washing` | **19.4 W** | 966 samples / 2,013 s. The base draws this while charging is also flagged on, so the charging branch is not added on top. |
| `self_wash_base_status = drying` + `charging_state = on` | **36.9 W** | 2,297 samples / 4,806 s. Total outlet power, not charging + drying. |
| `self_wash_base_status = drying` + `charging_state = off` | **6.3 W** | 98 samples / 204 s. |
| `charging_state = on` + battery < 100 % | **linear 15–99 %** | 2,150 samples / 4,486 s, 31.1 W average. Flat ~33.2 W from 15–92 %, then a per-level taper from 93 % (33.1 W) to 99 % (24.0 W). |
| `status = idle` | **14.6 W** | 752 samples / 1,568 s. The roughly 10-minute phase after a charge, before the robot reports `sleeping`. |
| `docked = true` | **2.8 W** | Settled standby: 2.83 W in `record-2`, 2.78 W in `record-3`. |
| fallback | **0.37 W** | Away from the dock (cleaning, returning, paused): 4,206 samples / 8,786 s. |

The charging curve uses one calibration point per battery level from the recordings. 0–14 % is a flat estimate at the 15 % value (32.83 W). The 18–73 % range was only recorded while mop drying ran, so it is interpolated flat between the 17 % (33.48 W) and 74 % (33.29 W) points; both ends are within 0.2 W, so the interpolation is effectively flat.

`min_version: v1.25.5` is required because the charging sub-strategy uses its own `entity_id` (the battery level sensor) inside the composite.

### Validation

Replayed against all four recordings (11,797 samples):

| Branch | Samples | Measured | Predicted | MAE |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| auto-empty | 47 | 414.52 W | 414.50 W | 203.90 W |
| washing | 966 | 19.33 W | 19.40 W | 4.19 W |
| drying while charging | 2,297 | 36.89 W | 36.90 W | 0.72 W |
| drying after charging | 98 | 6.25 W | 6.30 W | 0.60 W |
| charging | 2,150 | 31.28 W | 31.12 W | 1.45 W |
| docked idle | 752 | 14.58 W | 14.60 W | 5.59 W |
| settled docked | 1,281 | 7.10 W | 2.80 W | 4.89 W |
| away | 4,206 | 0.37 W | 0.37 W | 0.07 W |
| **total** | **11,797** | | | **2.47 W** |

Whole-run energy: **123.16 Wh measured vs 119.86 Wh predicted (−2.68 %)**.

The high auto-empty MAE is inherent to modelling a 6–17 s ramp as one average. Integrated over all episodes the branch matches exactly: 11.28 Wh measured against 11.28 Wh modelled. The settled-docked MAE comes from the intentionally unmodelled sleeping decay described below; the docked-idle MAE comes from the phase varying between 12.9 W and 16.9 W.

### Remaining limitations (documented in `model.json`)

- **The sleeping phase after the idle phase is not modelled separately.** Once `status` changes from `idle` to `sleeping`, the station still decays from about 17 W to 2.8 W over roughly 30 minutes while `status` is `sleeping` (mean 9.2 W). No entity distinguishes that decay from settled standby. The profile reports 2.8 W there, which under-counts the measured docked branch by **3.2 Wh per completed charge** (5.25 Wh measured against 2.07 Wh modelled over 44 minutes of docked samples). A time template on `charging_state.last_changed` was not used: it restarts on every Home Assistant restart or unavailable-to-off transition and would overstate power for a full window.
- **The transition at 100 % is not split out.** The charging branch stops at 99 %, so the short period at 100 % falls into the idle or docked branch.
- **Charging below 15 % and between 18 and 73 % was not measured in isolation.** See the charging curve note above.
- **Auto-empty is one average per episode**, not a two-phase ramp/tail model; the energy over the complete active interval is correct, the per-sample shape is not.

### Measurement notes

Powercalc Measure `v0.14.1` recorder with the vacuum recipe, about 2 s sample interval. The profile was replayed against all four recordings; the branch values and the whole-run energy are in the validation table above.

### Checklist
- [x] Single PR per device
- [x] Only `profile_library/dreame/RLE51SE/model.json` is added
- [x] Metadata complete: `name`, `aliases`, `compatible_integrations`, `product_url`, `device_specs`, `authors`
- [x] `measure_description` documents coverage and limitations
- [x] Generated and validated with Powercalc Measure
- [x] Schema validation against `profile_library/model_schema.json` (Draft 2020-12) passes; the workflow validator reports `success`
- [x] `min_version: v1.25.5` set for the per-strategy `entity_id` override
- [x] Replayed against all recordings, including whole-run energy
- [x] File ends with a trailing newline, LF line endings

### Generated files
- `profile_library/dreame/RLE51SE/model.json`

title: feat(measure): offer all relays of a multi-channel device
body:
### Summary

- Treat the sub-devices of one physical product as a single device when choosing relays, so a power strip or a 2PM can be measured in one run instead of one channel per run.
- Compare that physical device in the smart-switch preflight instead of the exact `device_id`.
- Hide configuration/diagnostic switches from relay choices.

### Problem

Home Assistant models a multi-channel device as one parent device plus one sub-device per channel, linked through `via_device_id` (verified on Core 2026.11 with a Shelly Power Strip 4 Gen4, model `S4PL-00416EU`):

```
shellypstripg4-48f6eedc7b7c              (parent, no switch entity)
shellypstripg4-48f6eedc7b7c Output 0     via_device_id -> parent
… Output 1 / 2 / 3
```

The smart-switch relay field is a multi-select grouped by device (`group_by_device`). Because each output is its own HA device, the picker offers exactly one relay per measurement, and selecting the others is impossible in the UI. A request that did carry relays from different sub-devices was rejected by the preflight with *"All selected relays must belong to the same Home Assistant device"*.

The same shape exists on the Shelly 2PM Gen4 (`S4SW-002P16EU`): parent *PV Akku*, children *Ladegerät* and *Wechselrichter*.

### Solution

- `EntityDescriptor` gains `device_group_id` / `device_group_name`: the root of the device's parent chain. Both `via_device_id` and the older `parent_device_id` are read.
- A child is only grouped with its parent when they belong to the **same product**: identical `model`/`model_id` and a shared config entry. A light connected through a bridge is also linked via `via_device_id`, but is a different product and stays ungrouped — this keeps `related_device_ids` and the vacuum dock handling untouched. `device_relations.py` is deliberately not changed.
- The smart-switch preflight compares `device_group_id or device_id`, including the existing "measure with an external meter, not its own sensor" guard, so a sibling channel's power sensor still counts as the device's own sensor and is rejected.
- `EntityDescriptor` also exposes `entity_category`; configuration and diagnostic switches (e.g. a Shelly BLE setting) are dropped from switch selections on both sides.
- Frontend: the relay device picker groups by `device_group_id` and lists the relays of the whole group.

### Files changed

- `utils/measure/measure/home_assistant/const.py` – `via_device_id` constant
- `utils/measure/measure/home_assistant/entities.py` – device groups, `entity_category`, switch filter
- `utils/measure/measure/ha_app/preflight.py` – group comparison in `_validate_smart_switch`
- `utils/measure/frontend/src/types/measurement.ts` – descriptor fields
- `utils/measure/frontend/src/components/setup/fields-section.ts` – group by physical device
- `utils/measure/frontend/src/components/setup/options.ts` – hide config/diagnostic controller entities
- tests: `tests/ha_app/test_preflight.py`, `tests/home_assistant/test_entities.py`

### Tests

- New: relays on sub-devices of one physical device are accepted.
- New: relays from two physical devices are still rejected.
- New: the catalog groups channels and names the parent device.
- New: a bridge-linked bulb is not grouped with its bridge.
- New: a configuration switch is not offered as a relay.
- Existing tests unchanged; the full Python suite passes (2,574 passed; the single remaining failure is an environment-only missing `custom_components/` in my reduced checkout and does not touch these files).
- Frontend typecheck passes. The frontend unit tests could not run on my machine (the bundler's native binding needs AVX, which this CPU lacks), so the built app was exercised in a Home Assistant app build instead.

### Manual verification

Home Assistant 2026.11.0, Powercalc Measure 0.14.3, Shelly Power Strip 4 Gen4:

- `/api/entities?domain=switch` now returns all four outputs under the parent device, and the relay picker offers `Output 0…3` together.
- A smart-switch measurement with all four relays produced `multi_switch` with `standby_power: 0.645`, `power: 0.572` and an all-on control reading of 2.89 W against an expected 2.92 W.
- On the 2PM Gen4, *Ladegerät* and *Wechselrichter* are selectable together and the BLE switch is no longer listed.

title: Add Shelly Power Strip 4 Gen4 (S4PL-00416EU)
body:
## Description

Adds a measured profile for the Shelly Power Strip 4 Gen4 (`S4PL-00416EU`), a power strip with four
individually switchable and individually metered sockets, using the `multi_switch` strategy. The
profile ships eight sub-profiles, one per measured device configuration (WLAN, ±Bluetooth, ±ECO,
±LED indication).

### Device information
- **Manufacturer**: Shelly
- **Model ID**: `S4PL-00416EU` (this revision only; `S4PL-10416EU` is a different hardware
  revision and is not covered by this profile)
- **Product name**: Power Strip 4 Gen4
- **Measurement device**: Shelly Plug S Gen3
- **Measurement method**: Powercalc Measure (app) 0.14.3, smart switch measurement type. The app
  build used locally groups the four relay entities of one strip into a single run, so all sockets
  can be measured together; the sampling, per-sample V^2/R subtraction and averaging logic is the
  stock implementation.
- **Mains voltage during recording**: 230.5 V to 231.7 V

### Recording coverage

Eight runs, one per device configuration. Each run measures six states - all sockets off, each of the
four sockets on its own, and all four sockets on - in three cycles with 12 samples per state at a
2 s interval, so 144 state means (1728 samples) in total.

The strip itself is the device under test, so a calibrated resistive dummy load (33.8 W, 1578.78
Ohm) sits in parallel on the same mains input and never on one of the strip's sockets. A Shelly
Plug S Gen3 measures upstream of both, the dummy load contribution is subtracted per sample as
V^2/R instead of a fixed offset, because it follows the mains voltage. The strip's sockets stayed
empty during every run.

All values are time averages over the windows in which the matching condition holds, not peak
values.

### Sub-profiles

| Sub-profile | Standby (all off) | Per switched-on socket | All four on, measured | All four on, modelled |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `+wlan` | 0.643 W | 0.494 W | 2.533 W | 2.619 W |
| `+wlan_+bt` | 0.673 W | 0.482 W | 2.572 W | 2.601 W |
| `+wlan_+led` | 0.660 W | 0.576 W | 2.931 W | 2.964 W |
| `+wlan_+led_+bt` | 0.686 W | 0.582 W | 2.959 W | 3.014 W |
| `+wlan_+eco` | 0.387 W | 0.471 W | 2.227 W | 2.271 W |
| `+wlan_+eco_+bt` | 0.454 W | 0.488 W | 2.351 W | 2.406 W |
| `+wlan_+eco_+led` | 0.360 W | 0.584 W | 2.596 W | 2.696 W |
| `+wlan_+eco_+led_+bt` | 0.488 W | 0.591 W | 2.748 W | 2.852 W |

In every sub-profile all sockets off, one socket on and the standby value match the measurement;
the deviation sits in the all-on state, see the limitations.

### Remaining limitations (documented in `model.json`)
- **The four sockets are modelled linearly** (`standby + n x power`), but the internal 5 V supply is
  shared. The measured all-on state is 0.03 to 0.10 W below the linear sum (1.1 to 3.9 %). The
  largest difference is 0.104 W, about 0.91 kWh per year with all four outlets continuously on.
  With one switched-on socket the model matches the measurement.
- **Two- and three-socket combinations were not measured separately.** The strategy only knows one
  increment per socket, so the interpolation between one and four sockets is not checked against
  the device.
- **The four sockets differ by at most 0.12 W within a run** (standard deviation 0.03 W or less),
  so a single increment per sub-profile is used.
- **The LED indication adds 0.08 to 0.11 W per switched-on socket.** The standby difference between
  LED on and off is within the run-to-run noise of about 0.03 W, which is why `+wlan_+eco_+led`
  (0.360 W) is not above `+wlan_+eco` (0.387 W). Values are reported as measured and the noise is
  called out here instead of being smoothed.
- **All values were recorded at a single mains voltage between 230.5 V and 231.7 V.** The firmware
  version of the strip was not recorded.

### Validation
Replayed against all eight recordings (144 state means, 1728 samples):

| Sub-profile | Off measured / modelled | One socket measured / modelled | All four measured / modelled | MAE |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `+wlan` | 0.643 / 0.643 W | 1.137 / 1.137 W | 2.533 / 2.619 W | 0.023 W |
| `+wlan_+bt` | 0.673 / 0.673 W | 1.155 / 1.155 W | 2.572 / 2.601 W | 0.015 W |
| `+wlan_+led` | 0.660 / 0.660 W | 1.236 / 1.236 W | 2.931 / 2.964 W | 0.019 W |
| `+wlan_+led_+bt` | 0.686 / 0.686 W | 1.268 / 1.268 W | 2.959 / 3.014 W | 0.019 W |

Not available: there is no Outdoor Plug S Gen3 in the Home Assistant instance this profile was prepared on. The model ID `S3PL-20112EU`, the SSID prefix `ShellyOutdoorSG3-` and the BLE ID are taken from Shelly's knowledge base (https://kb.shelly.cloud/knowledge-base/outdoor-plug-s-gen3).

## Checklist
<!--
  Please check all the boxes when applicable.
-->

- [x] I have created a single PR per device. When you have multiple submissions please create separate PR's.
- [x] The model name does not repeat the manufacturer name.
- [x] I have checked existing profiles for this manufacturer for consistent naming and metadata.
- [x] I have reused the existing `measure_device` value when my measurement device is already in the library.

## Additional info
<!--
  Add any additional info we must know about the measurements here.
-->

This is a **linked profile**, not a new measurement:

```json
"linked_profile": "shelly/S3PL-00112EU"
```

It keeps the Outdoor Plug under its own model ID `S3PL-20112EU` with a separate entry on the library website, while reusing the indoor Plug S Gen3 measurements. That is the approach requested in https://github.com/bramstroker/homeassistant-powercalc/pull/5046#issuecomment-6613983962.

**Relation to #5046:** that PR adds the same model with a single standby / standby-on pair measured with an AT35, and the question about the actual mains meter is still open there. This PR replaces that estimate with the measurements of the indoor Plug S Gen3. Happy to close this one if #5046 is preferred.

**Why the values are shared — manufacturer sources**

- Shelly's own comparison of the Gen3 plug family lists the Plug S MTR Gen3 and the Outdoor Plug S Gen3 identically in every row (relay, power metering, BLE gateway, Wi-Fi range extender, scripting); the only listed difference is the IP44 rating:
  - EN: https://support.shelly.cloud/en/support/solutions/articles/103000390376-comparison-of-shelly-plug-s-gen3-shelly-plug-pm-gen3-shelly-plug-m-gen3-shelly-outdoor-plug-s-gen3
  - DE: https://support.shelly.cloud/de/support/solutions/articles/103000390376-vergleich-von-shelly-plug-s-gen3-shelly-plug-pm-gen3-shelly-plug-m-gen3-shelly-outdoor-plug-s-gen3
- Both knowledge base pages publish the **identical** "Simplified internal schematics" figure (same attachment file on both pages): https://kb.shelly.cloud/knowledge-base/shelly-plug-s-mtr-gen3 and https://kb.shelly.cloud/knowledge-base/outdoor-plug-s-gen3
- Identical ratings: 12 A / 2500 W, 44×44×70 mm, 60 ±1 g, `ESP-Shelly-C38F` with 8 MB flash, internal temperature sensor, AC voltmeter, AC ammeter and power/energy meters, SPNO relay with 10000 switching cycles.
- EU declarations of conformity No. 224 (Plug S Gen3) and No. 244 (Outdoor Plug S Gen3), both dated 2025-12-05, list the same harmonized standards.

Taken together, the identically documented capabilities, the identical internal schematic, the identical ratings and the matching declarations of conformity mean the metering path and the self-consumption of both models are treated as equivalent for this profile. I have additionally asked Shelly support for a written confirmation of equivalent self-consumption and will add it here when it arrives.

The documented differences are limited to the IP44 enclosure, a wider ambient range (−25…51 °C instead of −20…40 °C), the humidity range, the model string and the BLE ID.

title: Add profile for Shelly Plug PM Gen3 (S3PL-30116EU)
body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->
## Device information

Adds a profile for the **Shelly Plug PM Gen3** (`S3PL-30116EU`), a Wi-Fi plug that only measures
power and has no switching function. It is added as its own profile next to `shelly/S3PL-00112EU`
(Plug S Gen3), which stays unchanged.

- Manufacturer: Shelly
- Model ID: `S3PL-30116EU`
- Product name: Plug PM Gen3
- Product page: https://www.shelly.com/products/shelly-plug-pm-gen3
- Documentation: https://kb.shelly.cloud/knowledge-base/shelly-plug-pm-gen3

The device is a pure power meter: Shelly lists `PM1`, `PLUGPM_UI`, `WiFi`, `Bluetooth`, `Matter`
and `Script` as its components, with no switch. It therefore has a single operating state, so the
profile provides `standby_power` only — no `standby_power_on`, no switched output. It is registered
as `device_type: power_meter` with `only_self_usage: true`.

### Values

No separate measurement was taken on this device. The values are adopted from
`shelly/S3PL-00112EU`, which is built on the same Gen3 platform: both are documented with the same
`ESP-Shelly-C38F` MCU, the same 44 × 44 × 70 mm housing and the same meters (AC voltmeter,
AC ammeter, power and energy meters). From each pair of values in that profile only the lower one is
used, because it is the one that belongs to the single operating state of a device without a relay.

The sub-profiles are carried over with their original names:

| Sub-profile | `standby_power` |
|---|---|
| `+WLAN` | 0.62 W |
| `+WLAN +BT` | 0.67 W |
| `+WLAN +LED` | 0.76 W |
| `+WLAN +BT +LED` | 0.82 W |
| `+WLAN +ECO +BT` | 0.52 W |
| `+WLAN +ECO +BT +LED` | 0.70 W |
| `+WLAN +ECO +LED` | 0.38 W |
| `+WLAN +ECO -led` | 0.23 W |

`standby_power_estimated` is set, so the library website does not present these values as
measurements. The LED variants follow `PLUGPM_UI` `leds.mode`; the `power` mode (factory default)
was not part of the measurement series and is not modelled.

## Home Assistant Device information

Not available yet. The device is not (yet) part of my Home Assistant installation, so the model ID
and specifications are taken from Shelly's knowledge base and API documentation:
https://shelly-api-docs.shelly.cloud/gen2/Devices/Gen3/ShellyPlugPMG3

If a discovery mismatch shows up in practice, the model string is `S3PL-30116EU` and the device
name is `Shelly Plug PM Gen3`.

body:
<!--

-->
## Device information

Adds a profile for the **Shelly AZ Plug** (`S3PL-10112EU`), the Amazon/Alexa edition of the plug,
as a `linked_profile` to `shelly/SNPL-00112EU` (Plus Plug S).

- Manufacturer: Shelly
- Model ID: `S3PL-10112EU`
- Product name: AZ Plug
- Documentation: https://kb.shelly.cloud/knowledge-base/shelly-az-plug
- API docs: https://shelly-api-docs.shelly.cloud/gen2/Devices/Gen3/ShellyAZPlug

### Why a linked profile to the Plus Plug S

- The plug is a 12 A / 2500 W device with a single SPNO relay and 10 000 switching cycles.
- It has **Wi-Fi and Bluetooth only** — no Matter, no KNX, no scripting and no Wi-Fi range extender.
- Metering is the same set as on the Plus Plug S: internal temperature sensor, AC voltmeter,
  AC ammeter, power and energy meters.
- Measured values of `shelly/SNPL-00112EU`: **0.74 W** standby and **1.01 W** with the relay on.

The profile therefore only carries the metadata (name, alias, product identity, connectivity) and
links to the existing measurement, with `only_self_usage: true`.

## Home Assistant Device information

Not available yet. The device is not (yet) part of my Home Assistant installation, so the model ID
is taken from Shelly's knowledge base.

## Checklist

- [x] I have created a single PR per device. When you have multiple submissions please create separate PR's.
- [x] The model name does not repeat the manufacturer name.
- [x] I have checked existing profiles for this manufacturer for consistent naming and metadata.
- [x] I have reused the existing `measure_device` value when my measurement device is already in the library.

## Additional info

No separate measurements were taken; this is a `linked_profile` to `shelly/SNPL-00112EU`, so the
Plus Plug S values (0.74 W / 1.01 W) apply. Sub-profiles are inherited from the linked profile at
load time, so if `shelly/SNPL-00112EU` gets sub-profiles later, this profile picks them up without
any change here.

Known behaviour of `linked_profile`: when the profile is created, Powercalc merges the target's
JSON over the linking model (`json_data.update(linked_json_data)`), so `name`, `aliases` and
`device_specs` shown at runtime are the target's. Discovery and the library website use this
model's own entry, which is why the AZ Plug is registered with its own name and alias.

title: Add more sub-profiles SNPL-00112EU
body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->
## Description

Adds sub-profiles to the existing `SNPL-00112EU` (Plus Plug S, Gen 2) profile. The model currently
has a single fixed value pair; this PR splits it into **eight sub-profiles**, one per device
configuration (WLAN, ±Bluetooth, ±ECO, ±LED), measured with the same setup used for
`shelly/S3PL-00112EU`.

> **This replaces the current single-value profile, not a new model.**
> The model id `SNPL-00112EU`, its `aliases` and `legacy_ids` stay unchanged, so discovery keeps
> working. Existing installations will be asked once to pick a sub-profile, because the root
> `standby_power` / `standby_power_on` move into the sub-profiles.

### Device information
- **Manufacturer**: Shelly
- **Model ID**: `SNPL-00112EU` (covers V1 and V2, `SNPL-10112EU`)
- **Product name**: Plus Plug S
- **Measurement device**: GW Instek GPM-8310 for the original 0.74 W / 1.01 W root values; Shelly Plug S Gen3 for the eight sub-profiles
- **Measurement method**: manual for the original root values (transcribed from the linked video); Powercalc Measure recorder for the sub-profiles, with the stock per-sample V²/R subtraction and averaging
- **Mains voltage during recording**: 230 V
- **Plug firmware**: 1.7.6

### Values

| Sub-profile | `standby_power` | `standby_power_on` |
|---|---|---|
| `+WLAN` | 0.573 W | 0.870 W |
| `+WLAN +BT` | 0.595 W | 0.898 W |
| `+WLAN +LED` | 0.567 W | 0.981 W |
| `+WLAN +BT +LED` | 0.606 W | 1.021 W |
| `+WLAN +ECO +BT` | 0.392 W | 0.728 W |
| `+WLAN +ECO +BT +LED` | 0.428 W | 0.841 W |
| `+WLAN +ECO +LED` | 0.175 W | 0.569 W |
| `+WLAN +ECO -led` | 0.133 W | 0.451 W |

### Measurement setup

**Root values (0.74 W / 1.01 W).** These are the original values: manually measured with a
GW Instek GPM-8310, LED off, and transcribed from
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cLtao6yG7ds. V2 was added to V1 because the manufacturer does not
mention changes other than mechanical. They stay at the root for existing installations until a
sub-profile is selected.

**Sub-profiles (Shelly Plug S Gen3).** The plug under test and a calibrated resistive dummy load are
connected in parallel to the same mains input, and a Shelly Plug S Gen3 measures upstream of both. The dummy load is never connected
to the relay output, so the reference meter always sees the plug plus the dummy load and can
resolve the sub-watt self-consumption. The dummy load contribution is subtracted per sample as
V²/R instead of a fixed offset, because it follows the mains voltage.

All values are time averages over the measurement window of each state, not peak values.

### What changed

**Root `model.json`.** `standby_power` and `standby_power_on` stay at **0.74 W / 1.01 W**, the
original GW Instek GPM-8310 values, so existing setups keep working until a sub-profile is selected.
`config_flow_sub_profile_remarks` added; `measure_device` set to `Shelly Plug S Gen3` for the eight
sub-profile measurements; `measure_description` now documents both provenances. `name`, `aliases`,
`legacy_ids`, `gtin`, `product_url` and the existing author entry stay unchanged; Maxik933 is added
as co-author.

**Eight sub-profile directories**, same names and configuration semantics as
`shelly/S3PL-00112EU`.

### Device specifics of the Gen 2 plug

- `ESP32` with 4 MB flash (the Gen 3 plug uses the `ESP-Shelly-C38F`)
- 12 A / 2500 W, SPNO relay, 44 × 44 × 70 mm, 60 g
- Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, internal temperature sensor, AC voltmeter, AC ammeter, power/energy meters
- ECO mode is a `Sys` setting (`device.eco_mode`): it throttles the CPU and enables the wireless
  low-power mode, which is why the ECO variants are the lowest ones
- LEDs are configured through `PLUGS_UI` (`leds.mode`: `power` / `switch` / `off`); the factory
  default is `power`, which is not modelled — the `LED` variants use `mode = "switch"`, `No LED`
  uses `mode = "off"`

### Remaining limitations (documented in `model.json`)

- **The `power` LED mode is not modelled.** It is the factory default of the Plus Plug S, so a user
  running the stock LED behaviour has to pick a `+LED` or `+ECO +LED` variant, which matches
  `mode = "switch"` at full brightness.
- **Migration:** existing Powercalc entries for this model show a repair issue and need a
  sub-profile selection once.

## Home Assistant Device information

Shelly Plus Plug S (Gen 2), model string `SNPL-00112EU`, firmware `1.7.6`.

## Checklist

- [x] I have created a single PR per device. When you have multiple submissions please create separate PR's.
- [x] The model name does not repeat the manufacturer name.
- [x] I have checked existing profiles for this manufacturer for consistent naming and metadata.
- [x] I have reused the existing `measure_device` value when my measurement device is already in the library.

## Additional info

The root `standby_power` / `standby_power_on` (0.74 W / 1.01 W) stay unchanged and keep their
original GW Instek GPM-8310 provenance. The eight sub-profiles carry the new Shelly Plug S Gen3
measurements. In the ECO pairs the relay-off readings were transposed: `+ECO +LED` is 0.175 W and
`+ECO -led` is 0.133 W; `+ECO +BT +LED` is 0.428 W and `+ECO +BT` is 0.392 W. The LED-on variant is
now the higher one in both relay states, consistent with the on-state values.

title: Offer child device switches in the multi switch flow
body: ## Description Fixes the multi switch config flow for devices that Home Assistant splits into a parent device plus one child device per channel (Shelly 2PM Gen4, Shelly Power Strip, and any other integration that uses the same layout). Since 2026.8 the Shelly integration registers e.g. the 2PM Gen4 as three devices: the parent (`shelly`, `48F6EECD97B4`) and two channel children (`…-switch:0`, `…-switch:1`) linked through `via_device_id` / `parent_device_id`. Discovery already collapses them onto the parent (see #5024), so the user gets one discovery flow for the physical device — but the next step is unusable: **Before** `create_device_entity_selector()` builds the entity choice from `entity_registry.entities.get_entries_for_device_id(source_entity.device_entry.id)`, i.e. only the entities of the device the flow was started from. The parent device of a 2PM has no switch entities (the switches live on the channel children), so the multi switch step offers **no** switch when the flow starts on the parent — and only one when it starts on a child. In both cases the two relays cannot be selected together. **After** `create_device_entity_selector()` includes the entities of the structural child devices as well (`get_child_device_ids()`, following `parent_device_id`/`via_device_id` recursively). The flow started from the parent now offers all switches of the physical device: ``` include_entities == ["switch.channel1", "switch.channel2"] ``` ### Changes - `device_binding.py`: new `get_child_device_ids(hass, device_id)`, walks the device tree downwards (handles both `parent_device_id` and `via_device_id`, any depth). - `config_flow.py`: `create_device_entity_selector()` collects entities from the device and all its children, preserving parent-first ordering. - `tests/config_flow/test_virtual_power_multi_switch.py`: new test with a parent device and two channel children; asserts both switches are offered. ### Verification - `pytest tests/test_device_binding.py tests/test_discovery.py tests/config_flow` — **423 passed** - `ruff check` — clean - `mypy --strict` on both changed modules — clean - The new test fails without the production change (`FAILED … test_switch_entities_from_child_devices`) and passes with it. ### Scope Only the entity *choice* for the flow changes. Discovery behaviour and the profile library are untouched; devices whose entities all live on one device produce the same list as before. _This text was created with the help of my agent AI._

title: Show the session name while a measurement session is open
body:
Closes #5086

The session name entered at setup wasn't shown once a measurement was running, so several open measurements were hard to tell apart, especially across tabs. Following the suggestion in the issue:

- While a session is open (Measure, Result, Prepare, Submit profile), the header shows "Session" and its name above the progress steps. The current status, such as "Measurement complete", stays underneath in the panel.
- The browser tab title becomes `<session name> · Powercalc Measure`, and goes back to `Powercalc Measure` on the session list, setup and settings.
- Sessions saved without a name fall back to the product name, then the model ID.
- Long names wrap (`overflow-wrap: anywhere`), so a phone-width screen doesn't scroll sideways.

The change is in `components/app/shell.ts`, which already holds the snapshot for those screens, so the views themselves are unchanged.

Tests:
- Two new tests in `shell.test.ts` cover the name and title through the four screens and back to the session list, plus the product-name fallback. Both fail without the change.
- `npm test` (431 passed), `npm run typecheck` and `npm run lint` pass.
- Checked in Chrome against the e2e mock API at 1280px and 390px with an 80-character name, and ran the e2e suite. "shows record-more preflight errors … allows retry" fails intermittently at the `measure-running-view` step, at the same rate with and without this change (4 of 16 runs each).
